articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process

Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

Editorial Context: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.
• The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

fullParagraphs: West Bengal has witnessed a sudden, rapid spike in attacks on Christian home fellowships and churches since the summer of 2026, when the BJP government came to power in the State. Senjuti Sengupta and Shiv Sahay Singh report on the fear of the community that is less than 1% of the population in West Bengal

A 65-year-old woman, Purnima (name changed to protect privacy), had eagerly waited for October 31, 2026, when a new church was to be inaugurated in front of her house. Her family had donated a significant amount of land and the freshly painted white building of William Cary Memorial Church was ready to welcome devotees at Narayantala village in Basanti block of West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas district. Now, she shudders when she thinks about what happened on that Saturday afternoon to the church.

“The gate of the church was opened for the first and the last time on October 31. During the inaugural function, a group entered the premises and attacked the priests and others who were participating in the ceremony,” Purnima says, recalling the attack that left her and several others injured. She says she was hit with a stick and had to be hospitalised for a day. After the attack, the church has been closed, but Purnima says she often goes to its door to peek at the picture of Jesus Christ through a broken window.

fullParagraphs: SAD sources said that Mr. Badal is likely to leave for New Delhi after his rally at Raikot to meet Mr. Shah, with talks on seat sharing and finalising the alliance on the agenda

articles.title: Punjab Assembly polls: AAP releases second list of candidates
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two sitting AAP Lok Sabha MPs will enter the fray: Raj Kumar Chabbewal from Phagwara and Gurmeet Singh Meet Hayer from Barnala
The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Thursday (November 12, 2026) released its second list of thirty one candidates in Punjab for the upcoming Assembly election, due in early 2027.
Two sitting AAP Lok Sabha MPs will enter the fray: Raj Kumar Chabbewal from Phagwara and Gurmeet Singh Meet Hayer from Barnala.

The names were finalised after detailed deliberations with all members at a marathon meeting of the party’s Political Affairs Committee (PAC), chaired by AAP National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal, said a party statement.

The AAP has replaced Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian with his nephew Randhir Singh Dhira in Lambi. The party has also brought new faces as it replaced sitting MLAs in six other constituencies.

The party has made Karamjit Singh Rintu as its candidate from Amritsar North, following its sitting MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap’s recent resignation. In Jalandhar Central, Nitin Kohli has been named in place of Raman Arora and in Bathinda, Gopal Singh replaces Amit Rattan. In Patti constituency, Jassa Patti takes over from Laljit Bhullar while in Chamkaur Sahib, Jasvir Singh Garhi has been fielded instead of Dr Charanjit Channi.

The party made Parminder Singh Goldy as its candidate in Kharar replacing Anmol Gagan Maan. In Shutrana, former Shiromani Akali Dal MLA Varinder Kaur Loomba has been replaces with Kulwant Singh Bazigar.

On October 31, AAP released its first list of 40 candidates, all of them sitting legislators. There are 117 Assembly seats in Punjab and the five-year term of the Assembly ends on March 16, 2027. The AAP registered a landslide victory by winning 92 seats in the 2022 Assembly polls.

articles.title: West Bengal government to appoint coordinators if stay on civic polls not lifted, says CM Adhikari
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that his government would approach the Supreme Court with a Special Leave Petition (SLP) seeking that the stay on holding civic polls be lifted

The West Bengal government will appoint coordinators in the wards of Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Howrah Municipal Corporation if the stay on civic polls is not lifted by the Supreme Court, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The Calcutta High Court on October 6 restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming KMC elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.

Addressing a gathering in Howrah District, Mr. Adhikari accused Opposition parties of obstructing the electoral process, and alleged that residents had been deprived of elected civic representation and proper municipal services for years.

“Those who are likely to lose their security deposits in the elections are the ones obstructing the process,” the Chief Minister said. He said that similar to proposal at KMC, coordinators will be appointed for each ward in Howrah Municipal Corporation (HMC) if elections are not held in time. According to sources, BJP leaders are likely to be appointed as coordinators across KMC and HMC.

Mr. Adhikari said that his government would approach the Supreme Court with a Special Leave Petition (SLP) seeking that the stay on holding civic polls be lifted. According to the Chief Minister, officials have limitations and cannot provide civic facilities for a long time.

Elections to the HMC have not been held since 2013, and for almost a decade officials have been providing services to the people of the civic body. The Trinamool Congress run board at Kolkata Municipal Corporation was dissolved weeks after the Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power. Mayor of KMC Firhad Hakim and other councillors resigned and the State government appointed an administrator to run the affairs of the largest civic body in the State.

The Calcutta High Court on Friday (October 6, 2026) restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.

The West Bengal government had passed a legislation in the State Assembly on August 12, redrawing the wards of the KMC and HMC increasing the number of wards from 144 to 209 and 50 to 68 respectively. The Opposition parties have alleged the State government and its agencies have resorted to gerrymandering while undertaking delimitation of wards in order to secure partisan advantage to the ruling political party in West Bengal on the premise of previous electoral results.

The BJP government in West Bengal was keen on holding elections to KMC and HMC. In fact, the BJP leadership had started the process of selecting candidates. Mr. Adhikari has on several occasions, expressed their preference to hold civic body elections in Kolkata and Howrah by the end of November or early December this year.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that his government would approach the Supreme Court with a Special Leave Petition (SLP) seeking that the stay on holding civic polls be lifted

The West Bengal government will appoint coordinators in the wards of Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Howrah Municipal Corporation if the stay on civic polls is not lifted by the Supreme Court, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The Calcutta High Court on October 6 restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming KMC elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.

Addressing a gathering in Howrah District, Mr. Adhikari accused Opposition parties of obstructing the electoral process, and alleged that residents had been deprived of elected civic representation and proper municipal services for years.

“Those who are likely to lose their security deposits in the elections are the ones obstructing the process,” the Chief Minister said. He said that similar to proposal at KMC, coordinators will be appointed for each ward in Howrah Municipal Corporation (HMC) if elections are not held in time. According to sources, BJP leaders are likely to be appointed as coordinators across KMC and HMC.

Mr. Adhikari said that his government would approach the Supreme Court with a Special Leave Petition (SLP) seeking that the stay on holding civic polls be lifted. According to the Chief Minister, officials have limitations and cannot provide civic facilities for a long time.

Elections to the HMC have not been held since 2013, and for almost a decade officials have been providing services to the people of the civic body. The Trinamool Congress run board at Kolkata Municipal Corporation was dissolved weeks after the Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power. Mayor of KMC Firhad Hakim and other councillors resigned and the State government appointed an administrator to run the affairs of the largest civic body in the State.

The Calcutta High Court on Friday (October 6, 2026) restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.

The West Bengal government had passed a legislation in the State Assembly on August 12, redrawing the wards of the KMC and HMC increasing the number of wards from 144 to 209 and 50 to 68 respectively. The Opposition parties have alleged the State government and its agencies have resorted to gerrymandering while undertaking delimitation of wards in order to secure partisan advantage to the ruling political party in West Bengal on the premise of previous electoral results.

articles.title: TNPDCL seeks nod to procure 3,000 MW
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The TNPDCL, which submitted the proposal to procure 1,500 MW to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) in February this year, has now doubled the quantum
The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) has increased the quantum of its proposed power procurement from 1,500 megawatt (MW) to 3,000 MW through a medium-term tender agreement.
The TNPDCL, which submitted the proposal to procure 1,500 MW to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) in February this year, has now doubled the quantum.

A senior TNPDCL official said amid a power demand of about 19,000 MW and an extended summer, it has been proposed to buy 3,000 MW of round-the-clock (RTC) power for five years, under the Finance, Operate and Own guidelines.

TNERC will take up the application for medium-term power purchase, along with requests for deviation from the guidelines and permission to float a short-term tender to procure RTC and peak-hour power for the period from February to July next year.

TNPDCL submitted in its application that the annual power demand had increased to 22,000 MW from an average of 18,000 MW due to various factors, including changes in weather pattern, increasing migrant population, and a surge in electric vehicle sales, with the State set to face an energy shortage of 7,000 MW by 2029-30.
The senior official said the long-term power purchase agreements signed for a quantum of 2,830 MW would expire by 2028-29, prompting new procurement plans.
The estimated cost of the medium-term procurement is around ₹5.50 per kilo watt per hour, with the annual expenditure pegged at ₹6,150 crore.
When the State faced a power shortage this October, TNPDCL had to purchase power at a cost of ₹30 per unit to bridge the peak-hour gap.

articles.title: Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Microsoft said that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors”; it determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks

A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday (November 12, 2026), with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant's suite of apps.

Nearly 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.
Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services.
Microsoft said that it was investigating disruptions, notably related to its email and Teams applications.

In updates posted on social media, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.”

Microsoft later explained that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks.
Microsoft did not immediately provide more information around what might be causing that failure, but added that it was testing a fix.
“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” the Microsoft 365 Status account wrote on X.
Earlier in the day, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.

articles.title: India and U.K. are turning climate ambition into action
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The U.K.-India climate partnership shows what delivery can look like in practice. Both our countries recognise that the shift to cleaner growth is not separate from the pursuit of prosperity

Next week, Mumbai will become the stage for one of the world’s boldest climate ideas. The largest ever Earthshot Prize edition will bring together innovators, investors, businesses, policymakers and young people to turn environmental solutions into impact at scale. Five winners will each receive £1 million to accelerate their work.

It all began with a simple but powerful idea: that human ingenuity, innovation and optimism can help repair our planet. Founded by His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales, The Earthshot Prize seeks solutions capable of delivering transformative environmental impact. Since the Prize was launched in 2020, India has produced more Earthshot finalists and winners than any other country (nine finalists including four winners). This year two of the 15 finalists are based in India. As the Prize arrives in Mumbai, India’s growing influence in clean growth and climate innovation will be on full display.

articles.title: Eight-year-old undergoes endoscopic treatment for rare swallowing disorder
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The child, diagnosed with Type II achalasia, underwent a minimally invasive procedure at Rela Hospital in Chennai

An eight-year-old boy diagnosed with Type II achalasia – a rare disorder that affects the ability to swallow food and liquids – has undergone a Perora-l Endoscopic Myotomy (POEM) procedure at Rela Hospital.

Achalasia affects the nerves controlling the muscles of the oesophagus, causing the lower oesophageal sphincter – a muscular valve connecting the food pipe to the stomach – to remain abnormally tight. This prevents food and liquids from passing normally into the stomach. The condition is estimated to affect 0.1 to 0.18 children per 100,000 annually.

The child had progressively worsening difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids. Following the procedure, he was able to resume consuming clear liquids and subsequently, a soft diet, within 24 hours.

POEM involves passing an endoscope through the mouth and creating a small tunnel within the oesophageal wall to reach and divide the muscle fibres causing the obstruction. Unlike conventional surgery, the procedure does not require external incisions or stitches.

S.N.K. Chenduran, senior consultant and endoscopic surgeon, Department of Medical Gastroenterology, performed the procedure, which took about 50 minutes. He said performing POEM in children required particular precision because of the smaller dimensions of the oesophagus and the delicate tissues.

Dinesh Jothimani, director, Hepatology and Medical Gastroenterology, said persistent swallowing difficulties, regurgitation, vomiting, and unexplained weight loss in children warranted medical evaluation.

A 65-year-old woman, Purnima (name changed to protect privacy), had eagerly waited for October 31, 2026, when a new church was to be inaugurated in front of her house. Her family had donated a significant amount of land and the freshly painted white building of William Cary Memorial Church was ready to welcome devotees at Narayantala village in Basanti block of West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas district. Now, she shudders when she thinks about what happened on that Saturday afternoon to the church.

“The gate of the church was opened for the first and the last time on October 31. During the inaugural function, a group entered the premises and attacked the priests and others who were participating in the ceremony,” Purnima says, recalling the attack that left her and several others injured. She says she was hit with a stick and had to be hospitalised for a day. After the attack, the church has been closed, but Purnima says she often goes to its door to peek at the picture of Jesus Christ through a broken window.

Senjuti Sengupta and Shiv Sahay Singh report on the fear of the community that is less than 1% of the population in West Bengal

A 65-year-old woman, Purnima (name changed to protect privacy), had eagerly waited for October 31, 2026, when a new church was to be inaugurated in front of her house. Her family had donated a significant amount of land and the freshly painted white building of William Cary Memorial Church was ready to welcome devotees at Narayantala village in Basanti block of West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas district. Now, she shudders when she thinks about what happened on that Saturday afternoon to the church.

“The gate of the church was opened for the first and the last time on October 31. During the inaugural function, a group entered the premises and attacked the priests and others who were participating in the ceremony,” Purnima says, recalling the attack that left her and several others injured. She says she was hit with a stick and had to be hospitalised for a day. After the attack, the church has been closed, but Purnima says she often goes to its door to peek at the picture of Jesus Christ through a broken window.

articles.title: Sriperumbudur toll plaza gets MLFF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The scanners will read FASTag cards and number plates, and the system will automatically collect the amount due at the toll

Motorists using the Sriperumbudur toll plaza on the Chennai-Bengaluru National Highway from Wednesday midnight will be able to drive freely without stopping for boom barriers. . This is the second plaza in the State to get multi-lane free flow tolling, where gantries with scanners have been installed. The scanners will read FASTag cards and number plates, and the system will automatically collect the amount due at the toll. The facility will allow motorists to drive through, without having to wait at the plaza, which caters to over 1.25 lakh vehicles on a daily basis.

articles.title: Forming fact-finding panel by agitating students unauthorised, aimed at fomenting tension: SRFTI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, since September 27, has been investigated by a special investigation team constituted by the West Bengal government

SRFTI authorities said an independent fact-finding exercise initiated by a group of protesting students into the campus crisis was "unauthorised", claiming that such an attempt was aimed at "distorting the factual record, fomenting tension and undermining the ongoing SIT probe".

The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, said several incidents, including alleged attacks on students, since September 27 have been investigated by a special investigation team constituted by the West Bengal government, and questioned the legitimacy of a "parallel probe by an external organisation".
SRFTI Registrar Deepak Kumar said on Thursday (November 13, 2026) night that the institute had also constituted its own fact-finding committee to inquire into alleged violence on the campus.

"The matter is already under investigation by an SIT constituted by the West Bengal government. The institute has also constituted its own fact-finding committee to examine the incidents," Mr. Kumar said.
He alleged that the "parallel exercise is aimed at creating competing narratives, distorting the factual record and undermining the ongoing investigation".
Mr. Kumar alluded to a statement by agitating students to form a fact-finding panel on their part to probe the incidents, including alleged violence on the campus, since September 27.

"Such an attempt appears aimed at fomenting tension and keeping the issue alive rather than facilitating a return to normalcy," Mr. Kumar said, claiming that "using students to advance extraneous or political agendas" was unacceptable and detrimental to their academic interests.
"The institute will extend full cooperation to the SIT and expects all concerned to respect the established legal process," the SRFTI registrar said.
The institute has been witnessing protests since September 27 following alleged attacks on students during an RSS-linked Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat event on the campus.

The stir intensified after a second alleged attack on October 4 during a rally by Bangiya Hindu Jagran Manch, with students organising sit-ins and raising concerns over their safety, privacy and freedom of movement.

articles.title: A nonagenarian from Virudhunagar on a mission to spread Gandhi’s message
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: By contributing articles to Tamil journals, A. Pitchai, 91, has been spreading the importance and relevance of Gandhian thought since his retirement from service in the State government

Middle-aged persons may be contemplating taking early retirement from their work, but in Tamil Nadu, a nonagenarian from Virudhunagar district is not only physically and mentally active but also continues to write Tamil articles and launch books.

By contributing articles to Tamil journals, A. Pitchai, 91, has been spreading the importance and relevance of Gandhian thought since his retirement from service in the State government. Recently, he brought out a Tamil book on Gandhian philosophy, a subject that is dear to his heart. He is working on yet another book on the topic.

Born in February 1935, Mr. Pitchai, who was the first Director of the State government’s exclusive unit for the welfare of persons with disabilities after it was separated from the Directorate of Social Welfare in 1992, received a Ph.D. from the University of Madras, at the age of 70, for his study on Tamil Nadu’s experiences in rehabilitation management of persons with disabilities. A recipient of the State government’s “best social worker award,” the scholar of Gandhian philosophy has been serving, in his individual capacity, persons with disabilities through an organisation (Speaker Chellapandian Charitable Trust) instituted in memory of his father-in-law.

His latest book, ‘Gandhi Ennum Aarparithaadum Sol’, published by Sandhya Publications, contains articles carried by Tamil newspaper Dinamani between September 2021 and January 2026. Recalling Gandhi’s momentous decision in Madurai to change his attire to a simple dhoti and shawl from the elaborate Gujarati attire on September 22, 1921, the author suggested that the day be observed as a ‘day of simplicity’ and that the Tamil Nadu government organise an event to mark the occasion.

Another piece talks of Gandhi’s favourite devotional song, Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye , and its composer, Narsinh Mehta of Gujarat. One of the articles, published in November 2022, captures the plight of the Porbandar house where Gandhi was born, and calls for the early reopening of the structure that remained closed ostensibly for repairs. Mr. Pitchai also echoes the concerns of fellow Gandhians over the Gujarat government’s plan to renovate the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad and argues that in the name of redevelopment, the spirit and ethos of Gandhian simplicity should not be disturbed but preserved.

By contributing articles to Tamil journals, A. Pitchai, 91, has been spreading the importance and relevance of Gandhian thought since his retirement from service in the State government

Middle-aged persons may be contemplating taking early retirement from their work, but in Tamil Nadu, a nonagenarian from Virudhunagar district is not only physically and mentally active but also continues to write Tamil articles and launch books.

By contributing articles to Tamil journals, A. Pitchai, 91, has been spreading the importance and relevance of Gandhian thought since his retirement from service in the State government. Recently, he brought out a Tamil book on Gandhian philosophy, a subject that is dear to his heart. He is working on yet another book on the topic.

Born in February 1935, Mr. Pitchai, who was the first Director of the State government’s exclusive unit for the welfare of persons with disabilities after it was separated from the Directorate of Social Welfare in 1992, received a Ph.D. from the University of Madras, at the age of 70, for his study on Tamil Nadu’s experiences in rehabilitation management of persons with disabilities. A recipient of the State government’s “best social worker award,” the scholar of Gandhian philosophy has been serving, in his individual capacity, persons with disabilities through an organisation (Speaker Chellapandian Charitable Trust) instituted in memory of his father-in-law.

His latest book, ‘Gandhi Ennum Aarparithaadum Sol’, published by Sandhya Publications, contains articles carried by Tamil newspaper Dinamani between September 2021 and January 2026. Recalling Gandhi’s momentous decision in Madurai to change his attire to a simple dhoti and shawl from the elaborate Gujarati attire on September 22, 1921, the author suggested that the day be observed as a ‘day of simplicity’ and that the Tamil Nadu government organise an event to mark the occasion.

Another piece talks of Gandhi’s favourite devotional song, Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye , and its composer, Narsinh Mehta of Gujarat. One of the articles, published in November 2022, captures the plight of the Porbandar house where Gandhi was born, and calls for the early reopening of the structure that remained closed ostensibly for repairs. Mr. Pitchai also echoes the concerns of fellow Gandhians over the Gujarat government’s plan to renovate the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad and argues that in the name of redevelopment, the spirit and ethos of Gandhian simplicity should not be disturbed but preserved.

articles.title: C.S. Karnan, controversial former High Court judge, passes away in Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He was sentenced to six months of imprisonment during his stint as a judge of Calcutta High Court in 2017 after he passed an “order” sentencing the then CJI and seven other Supreme Court judges to five years of imprisonment

A controversial former judge of the Madras High Court C.S. Karnan (71), who was sentenced to six months of imprisonment in contempt of court proceedings by the Supreme Court during his stint as a judge of the Calcuttta High Court in 2017 and was jailed once again in 2020 pursuant to his retirement, died in Chennai on Friday (November 13, 2026).

According to sources, he breathed his last at a private hospital. A native of Karnatham village in Cuddalore distict , Karnan was born on June 12, 1955. He got enrolled as an advocate with the Bar Council of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on April 11, 1984 and practised in the Madras High Court, City Civil Courts and the Family Courts in civil, criminal, constitutional and service matters.

He was elevated as judge of the Madras High Court in 2009 pursuant to a recommendation made by the High Court collegium comprising the then Chief Justice A.K. Ganguly and Justices S.J. Mukhopadhaya and P.K. Misra and accepted by the Supreme Court collegium comprising of the then Chief Justice of India K.G. Balakrishnan and Justices B.N. Agrawal and Arijit Pasayat, the next two senior judges of the top court.

During his stint as a judge of the Madras High Court, Karnan had accused the other judges of ill-treating him because he belonged to a Scheduled Caste. He had also had confrontations, sometimes in the open court, with former Chief Justices R.K. Agrawal and Sanjay Kishan Kaul over recommendation of names to be elevated as judges of the High Court and alleged discrimination against scheduled caste lawyers.

Karnan was transferred to the Calcutta High Court on March 10, 2016. In February 2017, a seven-judge Bench of the Supreme Court led by the then Chief Justice of India (CJI) J.S. Khehar initiated suo motu contempt of court proceedings against him for levelling baseless charges against other judges and also restrained him from performing judicial as well as administrative work as a judge of the High Court.

On May 1, 2017, the Supreme Court had directed the West Bengal government to constitute a board of doctors from Pavlov Government Hospital in Calcutta to examine Karnan and report as to whether he was in a fit condition to defend himself. However, Karnan declined to be medically examined and gave a written declaration on May 4, 2017 that he was absolutely normal and with a stable mind.

On May 8, 2017, he passed an “order” sentencing the then CJI and seven other judges of the Supreme Court judges to five years of rigorous imprisonment and also imposed a fine of ₹1 lakh each under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act of 1989. He directed the Commissioner of Police, New Delhi to execute his “order” and granted liberty to the eight judges to approach the Parliament.

A day later, the seven-judge bench of the Supreme Court found Karnan guilty of criminal contempt and sentenced him to six months of imprisonment after observing that his conduct towards a large number of judges and judiciary in general had seriously blemished and tarnished the image of those concerned in particular, as well as the judiciary as a whole.

However, the West Bengal police could not execute the Supreme Court order since Karnan absconded and attained the age of superannuation on June 12, 2017. After an intensive search, the police arrested him in Coimbatore on June 20, 2017. Even after undergoing the sentence, Karnan continued to openly denounce large number of judges with allegations of corruption and caste based discrimination.

Around 10 criminal cases were registered against him for reportedly circulating 33 videos on the social media abusing sitting as well as former judges, their spouses, lawyers, court staff and others using “vulgar, scandalous, vituperative and obscene” words. The tenth case was booked for having allegedly trespassed into the residence of a former Supreme Court judge in Chennai and abusing her daughter and son-in-law in filthy language.

fullParagraphs: A suicide note has been recovered from the second-year UG student’s room, the police said

A 20-year-old student at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Roorkee, allegedly died by suicide on Thursday (November 12, 2026). The circumstances surrounding the incident are currently under investigation by the police, the university said in a statement on Friday (November 13, 2026)

Ayush Rajoria — a second-year student of the BS-MS Programme in Mathematics and Computing, Department of Mathematics — was allegedly found dead in his hostel room on Thursday evening (November 12, 2026).
A suicide note has been recovered from his room, the police said. Further investigation is under way.

“The circumstances surrounding the incident are currently under investigation by the police. The Institute is extending its full cooperation to the authorities and is committed to providing all necessary support to the family,” the university said in the statement.
The Institute also stands with the campus community and will extend necessary support to those affected by this unfortunate incident, it added.
Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the Tele-MANAS 14416 and Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050.

articles.title: Ernakulam Rural police in Keralam book 17,181 for traffic violations in 11 days
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Ernakulam Rural police have taken action against 17,181 vehicle owners for traffic violations during the first 11 days of November, with enforcement agencies launching an intensified crackdown on offenders following criticism over repeated fatal road accidents.

Of this, as many as 1,017 people were booked for drunken driving during the special drive. Action was taken against drivers of 1,316 vehicles for speeding and reckless driving. These included 278 buses.
Cases were registered against 25 buses for serious traffic violations.
The police have also recommended the cancellation of the driving licences of 66 people, including parents or guardians of minors caught driving vehicles.
Special teams have been deployed across all five subdivisions in the rural police district as part of the enforcement drive led by District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) K.S. Sudarshan.
“Checks are being carried out round the clock. Inspections are also under way at district borders, with police dogs deployed as part of the operation,” the police said.

A 28-year-old woman pedestrian was run over by a private bus near Kakkanad on November 4.
The Kerala High Court has repeatedly criticised the authorities over inadequate road safety enforcement and their failure to prevent reckless driving.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house

Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%

India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.
Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July.
“India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Microsoft explained that a portion of its infrastructure was 'experiencing elevated load' which it said was 'likely contributing to the connectivity errors'

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

“We’re seeing early stabilization and capacity improvements as recovery actions continue. To help preserve delayed mail during this event, we’ve extended email timeout to 48 hours,” Microsoft posted on X.

“When essential tools become unavailable, employees naturally look for ways to keep working,” Ben Mudie, field CTO of APAC Tenable, said. “The security risk is that temporary workarounds, such as personal email accounts or unapproved file-sharing services, can move sensitive business information beyond an organisation’s visibility and control. Disruption can also create opportunities for impersonation. An urgent request arriving through an unfamiliar channel, or a message offering to restore access, deserves extra scrutiny.”
He said that an outage alone does not establish that a cyberattack has occurred.

“But it does underline why business continuity and cybersecurity need to work together. Employees need clear, approved alternatives so they can remain productive without exposing company data or bypassing security checks,” he said.

“We’re seeing positive results for service stability and increased capacity as a result of our latest traffic optimization actions. We’re implementing these actions more broadly across affected regions as we seek to attain persistent recovery. A more comprehensive update can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin centre, as well as http://status.cloud.microsoft if the admin centre is not available to you,” the company said in a statement.

From Asia to the U.S., Microsoft’s outage involving services like Outlook and Teams has dragged on for hours and impacted many users, companies and some government operations as the technology giant struggled with fixing the issue.
More than 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook earlier on Thursday although new reports have since fallen from that peak.
Singapore’s Government Technology Agency said that government emails were down and that the agency is working with Microsoft to resolve the issue.

articles.title: COP31: Himalayan flash floods should push all to act ‘faster and fairer’ on climate change: UN climate chief
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: “The glacial collapse and flash floods in the Himalayas this year are a devastating reminder of how fragile these mountain environments can be, particularly the Hindu Kush Himalayas,” UNFCCC Executive Secretary Simon Stiell said
The glacial collapse and flash floods in the Himalayas this year should push everyone to act "faster and fairer" on climate change, a top United Nations official said.

Responding to a question on the issue of the Himalayas on the sidelines of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya,Turkiye, United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Executive Secretary Simon Stiell told PTI that transitioning away from fossil fuels in a just, orderly and equitable manner, along with tripling adaptation finance, are key to resolving the crisis.

“The glacial collapse and flash floods in the Himalayas this year are a devastating reminder of how fragile these mountain environments can be, particularly the Hindu Kush Himalayas. For years, scientists and local communities have been warning that the Himalayas are at huge risk from climate change. What is happening in the Himalayas should push us to act faster and fairer on climate change,” he said.
Proposals by Nepal and Bhutan, and separately by Kyrgyzstan, to secure formal agenda items on mountain-related issues at the 31st UN failed to secure the backing of major negotiating blocs.
COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts
World leaders take stage at COP31 but big names missing

Highlighting that global heating is caused by humanity still burning huge amounts of coal, oil and gas and destroying forests, the UNFCCC Executive Secretary recalled COP28 in the UAE, where all countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems in a just, orderly and equitable manner.

He stated that the agreement must be delivered in full, and that it is equally essential to make faster progress on helping nations adapt to climate impacts and build their resilience, especially vulnerable nations that did practically nothing to contribute to the climate crisis.

“That means delivering in full on the tripling of adaptation finance agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year. Full delivery on all existing financial commitments by developed economies is also essential, as is boosting access to finance for those who need it most, especially those vulnerable developing nations who did the least to cause the global crisis,” Mr. Stiell told PTI .

When asked how climate-vulnerable nations can trust a platform like COP given that the agenda on tripling adaptation finance failed to be formally adopted, he said that the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) has been set up to provide support to vulnerable developing countries, adding that the crisis in the Himalayas shows why the COP process is critical.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV denounces ‘machismo,’ demands women be protected in emotional return to Peru
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Pope Leo called on the influential Catholic hierarchy to be models of unity and communion, and instructed Peruvian bishops to accompany their flocks and respond to victims of clergy sexual abuse with truth and justice

Pope Leo XIV on Thursday (November 12, 2026) denounced widespread “machismo” and violence against women in Peru, demanding that women be protected and respected as he set out marching orders for his beloved Peruvian church and people.
After his emotional homecoming Wednesday (November 11, 2026), the Peruvian Pope got down to business and turned to the challenges facing a church and country he knows well.

He called on the influential Catholic hierarchy to be models of unity and communion, and instructed Peruvian bishops to accompany their flocks and respond to victims of clergy sexual abuse with truth and justice. He also met with six survivors, including from an abusive sect-like group that Pope Francis suppressed last year.

But the 71-year-old Pope also showed himself to be positively overjoyed to be home and as relaxed as he has been in public since his 2025 election.

The Pope sang along enthusiastically as 40,000 people in Lima's Plaza Mayor serenaded him with “Contigo Peru,” a famous song from Peru's Pacific coast that celebrates national unity. He sang along later to another hymn, Alma Misionera (Missionary Soul), in Lima's stadium during a vigil along with 60,000 people inside and another 300,000 outside, according to Vatican estimates.

He said he left his home at 3 a.m. local time to go to the historic centre and stand in line to get as close as possible to the Pope.

Zozimo Perez came in a self-designed costume he named “the Inca Warrior,” with the pontiff's image on his chest and back. He was in tears as he saw Pope Leo stroll around the square. “This is a gift from heaven,” he said.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Microsoft explained that a portion of its infrastructure was 'experiencing elevated load' which it said was 'likely contributing to the connectivity errors'

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

European stock market operator Euronext advised listed companies on Friday (November 13, 2026) morning to ‌use the telephone to communicate corporate information after ⁠an outage in Microsoft’s Outlook email service.

“Euronext Corporate Actions and Listing ‌teams are currently experiencing an email communication ‌disruption and are unable to ‌receive ⁠emails,” the company, which ⁠runs exchanges in Paris, Brussels, Lisbon, Amsterdam, Oslo, Athens and Milan, said in a ‌corporate filing.

“For urgent matters relating to suspensions, corporate actions management, Oslo major shareholding ‌notifications, MyEuronext or Newspoint, issuers and their agents are advised to contact the ⁠relevant Exchange Operator by telephone,” it added.
The company ‌advised MyEuronext users to call through mobile phones and use two-factor authentication. Euronext did not say how it would guarantee ‌safe identification of other callers.

The U.K.’s National Health Service (NHS) is facing issues with emails due to the Microsoft outage, reports The Guardian . Earlier, NHS England signed a major five-year deal to use Microsoft 365. Doctors are trying to keep things running as normal.

“We’re seeing early stabilization and capacity improvements as recovery actions continue. To help preserve delayed mail during this event, we’ve extended email timeout to 48 hours,” Microsoft posted on X.

“When essential tools become unavailable, employees naturally look for ways to keep working,” Ben Mudie, field CTO of APAC Tenable, said. “The security risk is that temporary workarounds, such as personal email accounts or unapproved file-sharing services, can move sensitive business information beyond an organisation’s visibility and control. Disruption can also create opportunities for impersonation. An urgent request arriving through an unfamiliar channel, or a message offering to restore access, deserves extra scrutiny.”
He said that an outage alone does not establish that a cyberattack has occurred.

articles.title: Who is Colette Kress? Nvidia's new interim CEO following Jensen Huang’s exit
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A 13-year Nvidia veteran, Colette Kress will lead the chipmaker whose processors power cutting-edge AI data centers and supercomputers, as the board weighs a longer-term successor.

Nvidia co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday (November 13, 2026), following reports of two extramarital affairs, one involving an Nvidia executive who reported to him and another involving a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. While Mr. Huang apologised for being unfaithful and Nvidia investigates whether he was targeted by foreign intelligence, the chipmaker’s shares have tumbled more than 30% from their October peak.

In a bid to reclaim control, Nvidia's finance chief, Colette Kress, will assume the role of interim CEO, taking over from Mr. Huang, the company announced on Thursday (November 12, 2026). This will put her in charge of the chipmaker whose processors ​power the world’s most advanced supercomputers and AI data centers.

Ms. Kress is far from an outsider to the $4 trillion AI mammoth in the artificial intelligence industry. She joined Nvidia in September 2013 ​as executive vice president and chief financial officer and has held the post since. ​She has appeared alongside Mr. Huang on the company’s quarterly earnings calls. Prior to joining Nvidia, Ms. Kress worked at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments.
Nvidia’s ⁠revenue was $4.13 billion in the fiscal year she joined and $215.9 billion in fiscal 2026.

Before Nvidia, Ms. Kress spent nearly 25 years building her career at some of the tech sector’s biggest giants. She started out with an eight-year stint in finance roles at Texas Instruments before moving to Microsoft, where she worked from 1997 to 2010 and became CFO of the server amd Tools division.

She moved to Cisco (CSCO.O) in 2010 as senior vice president ​and chief financial officer of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organisation, where she was ​responsible for financial strategy and business development. She left for Nvidia in 2013, eventhough Nvidia was the smallest company she had ever worked for.
She holds a bachelor’s degree finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

Nvidia’s stock rise over the past decade made Ms. Kress one fo the wealthiest executives in the world. Forbes ranked her No. 32 on its 2026 list of America’s richest self-made women. At the stock’s October peak, her Nvidia holdings pushed her personal net worth past $1 billion, though the recent market slide reduced her company shares to roughly $750 million. She was awarded a pay package worth $14 million for Nvidia’s fiscal 2026, according to Nvidia’s proxy statement. This also includes restricted stock units.

Executive officers at Nvidia are employed at will and have no ​individual employment, severance or change-in-control agreements, according to the company’s proxy ​statement. Nvidia ⁠has said in earlier filings that many of its peer companies offer such agreements.
In a statement on Thursday, Ms. Kress said that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she would build on the “extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.”

articles.title: What are the findings of the 2024 Hindu Kush Himalayas snow update? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: What does the report by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development highlight? How important is snow persistence? How much of a role does climate change play in river basins receiving low levels of snowmelt this year?

T he Ganga river basin — India’s largest — reached a record low snow persistence in 2024, the Hindu Kush Himalaya snow update of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) has reported. The Brahmaputra and the Indus basins have suffered similarly, threatening water supply to millions of people. “Tragically this is yet another postcard from the frontlines of a climate crisis that is accelerating even beyond scientists’ projections and causing huge challenges in one of the most populated regions of the world,” Miriam Jackson, Cryosphere Lead at ICIMOD and a contributor to reports of the UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, told The Hindu .

Snow persistence is the fraction of time snow is on the ground. When this snow melts, it provides water to people and ecosystems. In the river basins of the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH), snowmelt is the biggest source of water in the streams. Overall, it contributes 23% of the runoff to the region’s 12 major river basins every year. The HKH mountains extend around 3,500 km over eight countries — Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Nepal, Myanmar, and Pakistan. These mountains are also called the “water towers of Asia” because they are the origins of 10 crucial river systems on the continent — Amu Darya, Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra, Irrawaddy, Salween, Mekong, Yangtse, Yellow river, and Tarim. These river basins provide water to almost one-fourth of the world’s population and are a significant freshwater source for 240 million people in the HKH region.

The authors of the 2024 HKH snow update analysed data from 2003 to 2024 and found significant fluctuations in snow persistence between November and April every year, when snow accumulates above ground. Based on this, they made grim predictions of lasting impact on the people in the region as well as those downstream of the river basins.

In India, snow persistence in the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Indus river basins dropped significantly in 2024. The Ganga river basin noted its lowest snow persistence in 22 years, 17% below the long-term historical average (also known as ‘normal’). The previous holder of this dubious distinction was 2018, when it was 15.2% below normal. In 2015, on the other hand, snow persistence was 25.6% above normal.

These river basins provide water to almost one-fourth of the world’s population and are a significant freshwater source for 240 million people in the HKH region.

“Due to changing climate and global warming, this pattern is becoming increasingly unstable. articles.title: Jewellery and souvenir made from plastic discarded in the Himalayas
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Plastic bottle caps left by climbers in the Himalayas are repurposed by Moware into mini Himalayan models, rocks of Himalayas, jewellery, and more

Have you ever wondered what happens to discarded plastic bottle caps? At best, they transform into wheels in DIY toy projects; or so we think. In Nepal, they are recycled into souvenirs, jewellery and everyday utility items by Nepal-based Moware. This design intervention enterprise Eva Villardon Grande gives a new meaning to waste left behind in the Himalayas.

Launched in 2013, Moware which stands for ‘Mountain Waste Repurpose’, employs innovative ways to reduce our footprint by upcycling and creatively transforming waste into useful products. The initiative was kickstarted to promote paper waste management in offices, even as it generated employment for low-income women from Lalitpur, Kathmandu. Over the years, they diversified, experimenting extensively with waste aluminium, wrappers, and glass bottles.
The Himalayan stones - Renjo La, Cho La and Kongma La | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Among their collectables, the most talked about is the From the Himalayas collection including a miniature model of the mountains that shows its most iconic peaks — Shartse, Lhotse, Mount Everest, Nuptse, Changtise Peak, Khumbutse Peak, and Mount Lingtren. The collection also includes ornamental rocks, jewellery and candle stand, all made from plastic bottle caps discarded by trekkers in the Himalayas.
Plastic bottle caps at Moware’s workshop | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

The glass in the collection are made from recycled alcohol bottles that are left behind by tourists. These are collected from hotels by Waste management companies. Moware sources these and turns them into utility items. An average trekker uses approximately 38 water bottles during the climb. Moware decided to see what could be done with the plastic instead of sending it to landfills, or having it incinerated. Towards this end, they set out to collaborate with two like-minded waste product resource management companies, Blue Waste and Sagarmatha Next., based out of Nepal, to find a solution.

Carry Me Back was the first initiative of Sagarmatha Next to address the waste management challenge in the Sagarmatha National Park and the Khumbu region (Nepalese side of Mount Everest). When the pilot project of the crowdsourced waste removal system was initiated in 2019, 2,500 tourists transported about 4,000 kilograms of waste. The waste is segregated, packed in specially made bags and left at a pick-up station located by the stupa in Namche Bazaar.
Eva and her team members at Moware | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Why bottle caps? Eva explains, “While a plastic bottle without the cap may have a lot of takers, the plastic cap itself — made from High-Density Polyethylene (HDP) — finds no takers, so they eventually end up in landfills.”

Moware then collaborated with Pim and Luc of Super Local, a team of Dutch designers based in Nepal. The duo devoted themselves to reducing waste and creating sustainable products hand-in-hand with local communities. “After a few months of brainstorming, they devised the Himalayan model design and Himalayan stones. The Himalayan stone are assortment of three mani stones — Renjo La, Cho La and Kongma La. These stones represent the awe-inspiring three passes of the Khumbu region. We just loved it and saw a beautiful chance to give the caps a new life,” says Eva who has made Nepal her home for now, to work on similar projects.

articles.title: Proof of allegations against Modi on my phone, which PM taps: Rahul Gandhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rahul Gandhi has repeatedly challenged Narendra Modi to an open debate and earlier claimed that it would take him just five minutes to establish that the Prime Minister was a “traitor”.

Upping the ante over his debate dare to Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday (November 13, 2026) alleged that he has proof of allegations against Mr. Modi on his phone, which is being “tapped by the prime minister”.
Mr. Gandhi also claimed that a one-on-one debate with him will end Mr. Modi’s political career.

Responding to a question during an ‘Ask Me’ session on Instagram about why he was insisting on a public debate when the BJP has said that the exchange can take place in Parliament, Mr. Gandhi said he was not allowed to speak in the House, and his microphone was even switched off.

“You did not let me talk on the farm bills, vote chori, SIR, China, on (Gen) Naravane’s book, Epstein. I want a one-on-one debate. I don’t want a debate entailing long speeches,” the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha said.

“I want that Narendra Modi makes allegations against me and I do the same to him. He can come; there will be a table, on one side there will be Narendra Modi ji and on the other side, it will be me,” Mr. Gandhi said.
He added that he had no objection if Adani Group chairperson Gautam Adani or RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat was appointed as the judge for the debate.
“But I guarantee that the prime minister will not remain the PM after a one-on-one debate with me,” Mr. Gandhi said.
Responding to another question during the session, Gandhi said the proof of all his allegations is on his phone, “which is tapped by the prime minister”.
He alleged that a one-on-one debate would establish who was controlled by foreign powers and who was an “anti-national”, adding that his phone contained details about these matters.
Posting a video on X, Mr. Gandhi also claimed, “The prime minister’s political career will be over if he comes and debates with me; he knows that and I know that.”

articles.title: No differences with Keralam CM over power procurement, says Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sunny Joseph said there was no immediate power crisis, but the government could not ignore the increasing demand, particularly during the summer months

Keralam Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph on Friday said there were no differences between him and Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan over power procurement and that the government was continuing efforts to secure electricity through long-term agreements to meet the State's growing demand.
Responding to reporters' queries here, Mr. Joseph said there was no immediate power crisis, but the government could not ignore the increasing demand, particularly during the summer months.
He also clarified that the State had not entered into any agreement with private power procurement platform GNA and that there were no immediate plans to proceed with such a deal.

articles.title: Shashi Tharoor alleges 115 Bharat Summit speakers barred entry to India, their visas cancelled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The senior Congress leader said the summit would also focus on establishing a think tank ‘Our World Institute’, and creating a platform for dialogue and cooperation between the Global South and the Global North

Senior Congress leader and MP Shashi Tharoor has alleged that 115 of the 315 speakers invited to the second edition of the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad were denied entry into India or had their visas cancelled, “apparently on the instructions of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs”.

Mr. Tharoor, who is in Hyderabad for the Bharat Summit, in a post on social media platforms, questioned the legal basis for the action and said it was unclear under which provision of law the government had taken such a step. He pointed out that the summit would conclude on Saturday (November 14, 2026), making it impossible to reverse the decision in time for the affected participants to attend.
“What a shame that a proud democracy has become so insecure that it must stifle any voices it fears will be critical!” he wrote.

His allegations came in the wake of a Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng claiming that she had been advised by the Indian Embassy not to travel to India despite holding a valid visa to participate in the summit. She works for the Oslo-based newspaper Dagsavisen.

Earlier, Congress MP and Telangana Congress media in-charge Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy had also alleged that nearly 30% of the invitees could not travel to India because of visa-related issues. Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi is scheduled to participate in the valedictory session on Saturday.

The controversy has raised questions over the participation of international delegates at the two-day summit, which seeks to bring together nearly 1,000 participants from India and around 70 countries. The event is being held against the backdrop of the 80th year of India’s Independence and the 137th birth anniversary of the country’s first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
Mr. Tharoor said the summit would also focus on establishing a think tank, ‘Our World Institute’, and creating a platform for dialogue and cooperation between the Global South and the Global North.

The allegations come amid political controversy over the event, with the BJP calling it an “anti-India summit” and accusing Mr. Gandhi of giving a platform to forces opposed to the country’s interests. BJP leaders in Telangana have announced plans to protest against his visit to Hyderabad.

Union Coal Minister G. Kishan Reddy, addressing a press conference in New Delhi on Thursday, termed the Bharat Summit an “anti-India summit”. The BJP alleged the event was meant to bring together forces critical of India and questioned the Congress leadership’s motives for organising it.

Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao questioned the rationale behind holding such an event in the State when the government was facing financial constraints. He accused Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy of spending public money to sponsor what he described as anti-India forces, in order to please Mr. Rahul Gandhi.
