articles.title: Offering food, best dharma
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Offering food to others is the best dharma, said R. Narayanan in a discourse. There is nothing to equal this, says Tiruvalluvar. In his Tirumanthiram, Tirumoolar says we should offer a vilva leaf to Lord Siva, grass to a cow, and food to fellow human beings. More importantly, we must always use sweet words. Tiruvalluvar says that even nectar, which confers immortality, must be shared with others.

Ilayankudi Maranar was one of the 63 Nayanmars praised by Sekkizhar in his Periya Puranam. Maranar was wealthy. He honoured devotees of Siva by washing their feet with scented water. He then offered them a lavish meal, which did not lack any flavour. The Lord wanted to show the world how generous Ilayankudi Maranar could be even in poverty. He made sure that Maranar lost his wealth. Eventually, he was left with nothing but a tiled house and a small plot of land. One night, after Maranar had sown seeds in his field, it rained heavily. That night, Siva, in the guise of a Saivite devotee, arrived at Maranar’s doorstep. Maranar’s wife asked her husband to fetch the grains that had been sown that morning. She cleaned the grains, and used it to cook rice for the visitor. Usually, the grains used for sowing were never used for cooking, because they ensured that a farmer would be able to grow his next crop. So, something that would take care of a farmer’s future would never be used for food. But Maranar and his wife broke that rule, when they cooked for the mendicant. Greens grown in the backyard were also used to prepare tasty dishes. Since there was no firewood, Maranar’s wife used a wooden beam from their house as firewood. When the couple was about to serve food, the sleeping guest woke and revealed Himself as Lord Siva. He blessed them and said they would reach Sivaloka.
Political & National Report: Offering food, best dharma. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Haryana Congress to launch campaign to protect people’s voting rights, says Sanjay Dutt
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: All India Congress Committee Haryana in-charge Sanjay Dutt and Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee president Rao Narender Singh will lead the two-week tour, participating in ‘Chaupals’ (community gatherings)

Haryana Congress will launch ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ campaign from November 12 to November 24 in the State, for what it terms an initiative to defend democracy, protect people’s voting rights and expose alleged electoral manipulation.

All India Congress Committee (AICC) in-charge of Haryana Sanjay Dutt and Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee president Rao Narender Singh will lead the two-week tour, participating in ‘Chaupals’ (community gatherings) across Haryana.
Mr. Dutt said the objective is to engage with people and mobilise public opinion in defence of democratic institutions and electoral integrity.

“The campaign assumes particular significance in Haryana, where the Congress party has raised serious questions about the integrity of the 2024 Assembly elections. Congress maintains that the people’s mandate in favour of the party was subverted through a systematic conspiracy of electoral manipulation,” he said in a statement.

“Our campaign will be much more than a series of public meetings. It is an initiative to take the fight for democracy directly to the people. Through these ‘Chaupals’, the Congress will expose electoral irregularities, sensitise citizens about the dangers of manipulated electoral rolls and build a statewide movement to safeguard every citizen’s fundamental democratic right to vote. We continue to reiterate the demand for the resignation and criminal investigation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The objective is unequivocal: every vote must be protected, every voter must be respected, and the Election Commission must function independently, impartially and without political interference,” he added.

Besides senior party leaders and functionaries, district Congress committee presidents, presidents and office-bearers of various frontal organisations, cells and departments from across Haryana will participate in this statewide campaign.

articles.title: Woman found dead at locked flat in Baranagar; police suspect sexual assault
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the police, the flat is owned by the victim’s sister and brother-in-law who had been staying there for the last four years. However, they had recently moved to Hooghly for their work
A 26-year-old woman was found dead at a flat in Kolkata’s Baranagar area on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) with the police suspecting she was sexually assaulted before the murder.
According to the police, the flat is owned by the victim’s sister and brother-in-law, who had been staying there for the last four years. However, they had recently moved to Hooghly for their work.

“Two days ago, her brother-in-law handed over the key to a lady. But the victim took the key from her on Tuesday and went to the flat at the fifth floor of the apartment,” said a police official from Baranagar Police Station.
Later, her sister was trying to reach out to her over the phone. But she did not respond to her repeated calls prompting her sister to inform the matter to the local police station.

Upon receiving the information, the police arrived at the apartment late on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) night and broke open the door to recover her body. “She was lying dead on the floor. There were also multiple injuries visible on her body. It could be sexual assault before the murder. However, the fact will be ascertained once we get the autopsy report. Further probe is underway,” said the officer.

Reacting to the development, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress alleged that the local BJP leaders are trying to downplay the gravity of the incident. “These are the very people who came to power promising women safety, chanting Bhorsha in, Bhoy out. Today, under their watch, Bengal has become a land of fear for women, where not a shred of trust remains in the administration. Failed CM. Failed investigations. Zero accountability,” it said in a statement on X.
The party also said that random encounters and case closures are no substitute for justice. “Where is the thorough investigation? Where is the accountability? Where is the deterrence?” it asked.

articles.title: Punjab polls: Congress begins campaign; BJP takes a dig
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh and Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the State Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa launched the campaign at the party headquarters in Chandigarh

Even as the Congress party on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) began its public outreach campaign — ‘Punjab Mangda Insaaf’ (Punjab Demands Justice) — in the run-up to the 2027 Assembly election, the Bharatiya Janata Party hit out at the Congress over its campaign, saying that a party, whose leaders were involved in anti Sikhs riots in 1984 has no moral right to speak about “justice” in Punjab.

Leader of Opposition in the Punjab Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa and Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee president Pargat Singh participated in a series of engagements in Mohali as a part of the party’s campaign, which the party asserts to aim to build a collective movement against the growing menace of drugs, crime, corruption and the deteriorating law and order situation in Punjab.

Mr. Bajwa said the campaign was not merely a political campaign but a struggle for Punjab’s rights, dignity and a better future. “The Congress would bring together every section connected with Punjab, demand answers from the Aam Aadmi Party government and present a development roadmap for 2027 based on suggestions received from the people,” he said.

Punjab BJP President Kewal Singh Dhillon, meanwhile alleged that the claims made in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s newly released memoir, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, concerning former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and the June 1984 Operation Blue Star, were calculated political ploy to whitewash the sins of the Congress.
“What does an ‘Insaaf Yatra’ mean in Punjab without full justice for the 1984 victims and a public, unconditional apology from Congress for its heinous crimes?” he said in a statement.

Mr. Dhillon alleged that for decades, successive Congress governments protected the guilty of anti-Sikh riots and handed out clean chits. “It was only after the Modi led BJP government took office in 2014 and constituted a dedicated Special Investigation Team (SIT) that justice finally caught up with the perpetrators,” he added.

articles.title: Keralam government centralising power in Chief Minister’s office: Pinarayi Vijayan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has accused the Keralam government of concentrating decision-making powers in the hands of the Chief Minister, alleging that even ministers are being kept in the dark about important decisions.
He said the situation was unprecedented in the State and called for a judicial investigation into what he described as suspicious administrative actions.

Speaking at the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] political explanation meeting at Chathurakkinar in Madikkai, Mr. Vijayan questioned how a Minister, who is also the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee president, could remain unaware of major decisions concerning his own department. He said governance was being conducted without proper coordination between departments, with the Chief Minister taking decisions independently.

Referring to the electricity purchase agreement with GNA, Mr. Vijayan said the Minister concerned had earlier said that he was unaware of the decision to enter into the agreement. The Minister was reportedly unaware even when the decision to abandon the agreement was taken, he said.
He also alleged that attempts were being made to create an artificial power shortage to benefit corporate monopolies.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: UN peacekeepers failed to protect civilians before South Sudan massacre: Amnesty
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: “Both the government and UNMISS had sufficient information and time to take more effective preventive action. Their failure to take stronger action cost lives,” said Tigere Chagutah, an Amnesty regional director

United Nations peacekeepers and South Sudanese authorities failed to take adequate action despite warnings weeks before insurgents raided a village and killed more than 200 people earlier this year, Amnesty International said in a report released on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The rights group said that the peacekeeping mission, known by the acronym UNMISS, knew that an attack on Abiemnom, a remote area near the border with Sudan, was likely but failed to reinforce the roughly three dozen peacekeepers based there until after it occurred.
Between 1,000 and 1,500 armed men from neighbouring Mayom County carried out the March 1 attack, shooting residents, burning homes and looting part of the hospital, Amnesty said.
The death toll was at least 213, according to authorities, including 130 town residents, 76 security personnel and seven foreign nationals.

“Both the government and UNMISS had sufficient information and time to take more effective preventive action. Their failure to take stronger action cost lives,” said Tigere Chagutah, an Amnesty regional director.

UNMISS spokesperson Priyanka Chowdhury said in a statement that the mission did its best with limited resources to provide protection and medical care to roughly 2,500 people who sheltered at a protected area established in anticipation of the attack.

Facing budget cuts and reduced personnel, she said that the mission "concentrated its available capacity on immediate protection of civilians seeking refuge within our base rather than dispersing limited forces across tasks they could not safely sustain simultaneously.”

The March assault came amid renewed fighting between government forces and an array of opposition groups, undermining a 2018 agreement that ended five years of civil war. The area has experienced cycles of retaliatory violence linked to land access and cattle raiding.
Amnesty said that the March attack may have been triggered by unresolved killings of several young men from neighbouring Mayom County in Abiemnom.
The investigation drew on interviews with 82 people, including survivors, witnesses and medical workers, along with satellite imagery and verified photographs and videos.

articles.title: Trump defends Iran war in Veterans Day address
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which “has been waging war on America since 1979”

U.S. President Donald Trump defended the war against Iran on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) at a U.S. Veterans Day commemoration that saw his Defence Secretary publicly admonished for a lack of decorum.
"The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible," Mr. Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington.
"When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better place, more peaceful place, and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer."

The war, which began on February 28 with U.S. and Israeli strikes against Iran, has so far cost the lives of 23 U.S. service members and wounded several hundred more, according to the latest Pentagon figures.

Mr. Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which "has been waging war on America since 1979." He stressed that U.S. forces were acting in order to halt Iran's capacity to build a nuclear weapon.
Mr. Trump, 80, attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery’s Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a sacred symbol for America's lost service members.

articles.title: VS Hospitals introduces digital mammography system for breast cancer detection
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The system uses a 50-micron detector to capture detailed images of breast tissue, helping radiologists examine tiny microcalcifications that may be associated with early breast abnormalities
VS Hospitals has introduced a new 2D digital mammography system to strengthen breast cancer screening and diagnosis.

The AMULET SOPHINITY system from Fujifilm uses a high-resolution detector with a pixel size of 50 microns, allowing detailed imaging of breast tissue, including tiny microcalcifications, which can sometimes be an early indicator of breast abnormalities.

Mammography uses low-dose X-rays to examine breast tissue and can help identify abnormalities that may not be detectable through physical examination. The new system has intelligent exposure control, which adjusts X-ray exposure according to breast composition while maintaining image quality. AI-based positioning support is designed to assist in accurate positioning and consistent image acquisition.

The equipment takes approximately five seconds for standard image acquisition and 12 seconds for high-resolution imaging. It also has features such as flexible positioning, intelligent breast compression and automatic decompression to help reduce discomfort during the examination.

Speaking at the launch, S. Subramanian, Chairman and Managing Director of V.S. Hospitals, said early detection was important in breast cancer care and that mammography played a key role in identifying breast abnormalities.
The hospital will offer free mammography screening to underprivileged people throughout November 2026. Those seeking to avail themselves of the screening can contact the hospital at 7448850500.

articles.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Chinese executive Alice Huang.

Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, are facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News . He graduated in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and later obtained a master’s degree from Stanford University, according to his Linkedin profile.

Mr. Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang. The Nvidia chief executive said he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he said in a statement posted on Nvidia’s website.
The New York Times reported that Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen allegedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Mr. Huang.

Mr. Huang also sent a message to Nvidia employees on November 8, 2026, acknowledging the affair and apologising to both his family and company staff. While expressing regret for his actions, he did not address allegations that Alice Huang was a suspected spy.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and alleged that she was providing information directly to Beijing.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on November 8, 2026. Independent directors have engaged external legal counsel to examine the circumstances surrounding the relationship. Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised, and that Mr. Huang would remain in charge while cooperating with the investigation.

Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen who was allegedly recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia chief executive, according to The New York Times , which first reported that Mr. Huang was the target of an alleged espionage operation.

fullParagraphs: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan told that the charge sheet was filed before a special court for POCSO cases in Chennai on November 11, 2026, and that the SIT intends to file multiple charge sheets in the next few days

A special investigation team (SIT) probing the serial child sexual abuse cases against Gem Granties founder R. Veeramani has already filed the first charge sheet in one of the multiple cases registered against him under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, and other laws, State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan told the Madras High Court on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP said, the first charge sheet in the case was filed before the special court for POCSO cases in Chennai on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) and that the SIT intends to file multiple charge sheets in some of the cases. He told the court that the charge sheets in other crime numbers would also be filed one after another in the next 10 to 15 days.

After hearing him, the judge adjourned a couple of connected writ petitions pending before him to November 30, 2026. He also perused a status report filed on behalf of the SIT, explaining to the court the progress made in the investigation so far, and told the counsel present in the court that he was satisfied with the substantial work done in the sensitive case related to sexual exploitation of children.

The judge directed the High Court Registry to keep the status report in safe custody and produce it before the court during the next hearing. The SIT had been filing periodical status reports ever since R. Varaaki and advocate M.L. Ravi filed writ petitions (criminal) in the High Court, seeking the transfer of investigation in the POCSO cases against Veeramani from the State police to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

After not finding any reason to order such transfer for the present, the judge had said that the SIT must be allowed to work in peace and called for periodical status reports on the ongoing investigation. When Mr. Varaaki’s counsel presented some evidence before the court on Thursday, the judge directed the petitioner to submit all those materials with the SIT instead of waiting for the court proceedings.

He also recorded the submission of the SPP that the SIT was also probing whether any of the police officials or others had ever tried to protect the prime accused Veeramani. When the judge wanted to know why the SIT should not conduct media briefings, the SPP said, the team was avoiding media interactions in order to ensure that sensitive information related to child sexual abuse does not get disclosed.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Today | Senior IAS officer sentenced to imprisonment for contempt of court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Welcome to the Tamil Nadu Today newsletter, your guide from The Hindu on the major news stories to follow today.

The Madras High Court, in May 2025 has found senior IAS officer and former Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) Member Secretary Anshul Mishra guilty of contempt of court and directed him to undergo simple imprisonment for a month.
Justice P. Velmurugan also directed Mr. Mishra to pay a compensation of ₹25,000 to elderly siblings who had been struggling for years to retrieve their valuable immovable property.
Later on June 12, 2025, a Division Bench of the Madras High Court suspended the sentence imposed by a single judge.

Months after, in September 2025, a Division Bench of the Madras High Court set aside the order passed by a single judge who found Mr. Mishra guilty of contempt of court proceedings and directed him to undergo simple imprisonment for a month.
Chief Minister M.K. Stalin left for New Delhi to take part in the 10 th Governing Council meeting of the NITI Aayog to be held tomorrow. The meeting will be chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Mr. Stalin was seen off at the Chennai airport by Tamil Nadu Ministers and DMK functionaries. DMK Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs received the Mr. when he arrived in New Delhi.
Later in the day, the CM met Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi at their residence.

S.P. Velumani, AIADMK MLA from Thondamuthur constituency in Coimbatore and former Minister, received an anonymous letter threatening to kill his family members and warning of a bomb blast in Coimbatore before July 30.

The letter, which was undersigned with the note “Allahu Akbar Pakistan Zindabad”, stated that three of his family members would be killed if a sum of ₹1 crore is not placed at a specific location in Coimbatore on May 25.

articles.title: Madras High Court suspends IAS officer Anshul Mishra’s one-month sentence in contempt plea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Division Bench of Justices M.S. Ramesh and V. Lakshminarayanan direct the officer to deposit ₹25,000 with the Registrar (Judicial) of the High Court

A Division Bench of the Madras High Court on Thursday (June 12, 2025) suspended the sentence of one-month simple imprisonment imposed by a single judge on Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Anshul Mishra after finding him guilty of contempt of court.

The Bench comprising Justices M.S. Ramesh and V. Lakshminarayanan suspended the sentence and directed the IAS officer to deposit ₹25,000 with the Registrar (Judicial) of the High Court within three weeks and without prejudice to his clean service records.

articles.title: Iran’s Guards say ‘accident’ left two tankers on fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that two tankers carrying over four million barrels of oil had caught fire after an "accident" on an unauthorised route in the Strait of Hormuz.
Since the outbreak of the war in West Asia in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic shipping channel, insisting vessels use routes it has approved.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.

"Last night, two tankers - acting in violation of regulations and despite repeated warnings from the Revolutionary Guards Navy regarding the unauthorised and dangerous nature of the southern maritime route - were involved in an accident while traversing this prohibited path in the strait," the Guards said in a statement.
They did not specify the nature of the "accident" but said it left the two tankers immobilised after they were hit with a "violent explosion".

"These two supertankers were carrying a combined total of over four million barrels of oil, which are now ablaze - a consequence of the blind trust placed in the aggressive American military," the statement said.
Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits.
Tehran has often said they struck mines, but the U.S. military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait.

articles.title: Alice Huang, accused of spying on Nvidia chief, entered Taiwan eight times in 2024-25: Official
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory

The woman accused of spying for Beijing during an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday (November 12, 2026).

Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory.

Jensen Huang, chief executive of the U.S.-based chip giant Nvidia, has admitted to having an extramarital affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who U.S. officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence.

Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan "under a standard business visitor status" and there were "no special flags" about her at the time, Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) Minister Chiu Chui-cheng told lawmakers.

Mr. Chiu made the remarks in Taiwan's Parliament in response to lawmakers' questions about Alice Huang's entries into Taiwan and a New York Times report that the United States had advised Taiwan as early as 2024 to monitor her movements.
"At least we at the Mainland Affairs Council did not receive any relevant information," Mr. Chiu said.
"If we had, we definitely would have stepped up our entry screening and border flow management."
Mr. Chiu said records show that Alice Huang visited Taiwan three times in 2024 and five times in 2025. The records do not show any entries for this year, he said.

"If we had any of the kind of critical intelligence you mentioned, leading us to believe she posed a threat to Taiwanese society, we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review," Mr. Chiu said.
"For any case where there are doubts, we intensify the level of scrutiny, and if we determine there are security concerns, there is no way we would allow her to enter the country."

articles.title: Sunita Williams serves as Grand Marshal at 107th New York City Veterans Day Parade
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The parade brought together veterans, military families, service members, marching bands, community organisations, and supporters to “recognise the courage, service, and sacrifice of America's military heroes”
Indian-origin NASA astronaut Sunita ‘Suni’ Williams has served as the Grand Marshal for the 107th New York City Veterans Day Parade.

Ms. Williams, a U.S. Navy veteran, was joined by thousands of American veterans, active-duty military personnel, marching bands, patriotic organisations, military vehicles, and participants at the annual parade honouring those who served the country through the years.
Addressing the gathering, which included Indian-descent New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Ms. Williams said she is “humbly honoured” to be at the 107th New York Veterans Day Parade.

“When I joined the military, I never thought for a moment that I would actually be a veteran...thinking you're so young and how you're going to conduct your life. But my first steps in the military showed me the foundation with which I led my life: courage, honour, commitment,” she said.
Ms. Williams also highlighted the opportunity she had to work and live in space with people from all over the world.

“I can't thank the military enough for the time I have spent, the lessons I have learned, and looking forward to giving those lessons to the next generation and seeing how they can do even more than we've ever dreamed of,” she said, adding that “exploration is in our heart and in our soul.”

“Freedom is not free, and we have shown that time and time again by being role models for the world in our journey for exploration and for brotherhood and sisterhood throughout this planet,” she said.

Separately, in a statement, Ms. Williams said, “It is an incredible honour to serve as Grand Marshal of the NYC Veterans Day Parade and to march alongside my fellow veterans. My time in the Navy shaped who I am and prepared me for every challenge that followed. I'm proud to join New Yorkers and Americans from around the country in honouring the service, sacrifice, and commitment of veterans from every generation.”
Grand Marshal Sunita "Suni" L. Williams takes part in a Veterans Day parade on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, New York City. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Mark Otto, President and Executive Director of the United War Veterans Council and U.S. Marine Corps veteran, said: “We are incredibly proud to welcome Suni as Grand Marshal of this year's NYC Veterans Day Parade on the 250th birthday of the United States of America."

articles.title: Xi says Taiwan 'reunification' must happen as history cannot be stopped
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, despite Taipei's strong rejection of that claim, and has repeatedly offered a "one country, two systems" model of autonomy

The tide of history cannot be ‌stopped, Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Thursday (November 12, 2026), as he urged complete "reunification" of Taiwan with ​the motherland and pledged to do so peacefully, making no mention of the use ⁠of force.

China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, despite Taipei's strong rejection of that claim, and has repeatedly offered a "one country, two systems" model of autonomy not supported by any major Taiwanese political party.
Resolving the Taiwan question is an "unwavering ‌historical mission" of China's Communist Party, Mr. Xi said in a speech in Beijing's Great Hall of the People.
"The tide of history cannot be stopped," Mr. Xi added. "The complete reunification of the ‌motherland must be realised, and it will certainly be realised."

Mr. Xi said China adheres to "peaceful reunification and the policy of 'one country, two systems'" and is willing to talk to Taiwan while upholding the "one-China principle", or Beijing's position that both sides ​of the Taiwan Strait are one country.
All ‌Chinese, including those in Taiwan, should join hands to jointly oppose Taiwan independence "separatist" forces and strive for peaceful development of cross-Strait ties, Mr. Xi added.
Taiwan's government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Despite Mr. Xi not mentioning the use of force, which China has never renounced for Taiwan, its military ‌operates around the island daily, and is extending its reach further into the ​Pacific.

Mr. Xi's speech comes a week ahead of the APEC summit in China's southern tech hub of Shenzhen, where he is due to ⁠meet U.S. President Donald Trump again, and also a little more than two weeks before important local elections in Taiwan.
Last month, Taiwan called on its people to steer clear of any of China's events to mark the ‌Sun anniversary, saying China had a distorted view of him and his legacy.

articles.title: OpenAI now allows enterprises to process AI requests within India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The facility initially supports GPT-6 Luna through OpenAI’s API, allowing requests to be processed and AI responses generated within the country to address enterprise data localisation requirements

OpenAI on Thursday (November 12, 2026) announced local processing and inference for its API in India , allowing eligible businesses and developers to have supported AI requests processed and model computations performed within the country.

The move expands the company’s existing data residency offering in India, which was introduced in May 2025 and allowed eligible customers to store their data in the country. The latest development extends this capability to cover where the AI model processes information and generates responses, addressing a key concern among businesses handling sensitive information.

Initially available for the GPT-6 Luna model, the new offering is aimed at organisations that have not fully deployed artificial intelligence in business operations because of requirements around where their information is processed. This is particularly relevant to customers in financial services with specific data localisation requirements, OpenAI said.

“Some Indian businesses have not fully deployed AI for important work because they need the information involved to be processed within the country,” said Nitin Bawankule, Head of Enterprise - India, OpenAI.

“Local inference gives them more control over where supported workloads run and helps address a practical barrier to adoption. It gives more businesses a way to put OpenAI’s tools to work, and gives Indian developers and startups more scope to build for their own, and enterprise needs.”

Under the new arrangement, both the processing of an API request and the model computation that generates its response will take place in India for supported workloads. Supported customer content will also be stored in the country, the company said.

The launch covers direct API usage and currently supports GPT-6 Luna input and output through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs. Customers can access the capability by creating a new API project, selecting India for both storage and processing, and using the corresponding India regional endpoint.

The development comes as OpenAI expands its presence in India. Earlier this year, the company introduced OpenAI for India, an initiative spanning AI infrastructure, enterprise adoption, skills development and local partnerships. The initiative included a partnership with Tata Group to develop domestic AI data-centre capacity, according to OpenAI.

OpenAI models were also made available for in-country inference through Amazon Web Services’ Bedrock platform. AWS announced the availability of OpenAI models on Bedrock in August 2026, including regional inference capabilities for supported models.
OpenAI said its now launched API inference residency offering is available in other parts of the world, with India, Australia and Japan among the latest markets to receive the capability.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action

The facility initially supports GPT-6 Luna through OpenAI’s API, allowing requests to be processed and AI responses generated within the country to address enterprise data localisation requirements

OpenAI on Thursday (November 12, 2026) announced local processing and inference for its API in India , allowing eligible businesses and developers to have supported AI requests processed and model computations performed within the country.

The move expands the company’s existing data residency offering in India, which was introduced in May 2025 and allowed eligible customers to store their data in the country. The latest development extends this capability to cover where the AI model processes information and generates responses, addressing a key concern among businesses handling sensitive information.

Initially available for the GPT-6 Luna model, the new offering is aimed at organisations that have not fully deployed artificial intelligence in business operations because of requirements around where their information is processed. This is particularly relevant to customers in financial services with specific data localisation requirements, OpenAI said.

“Some Indian businesses have not fully deployed AI for important work because they need the information involved to be processed within the country,” said Nitin Bawankule, Head of Enterprise - India, OpenAI.

“Local inference gives them more control over where supported workloads run and helps address a practical barrier to adoption. It gives more businesses a way to put OpenAI’s tools to work, and gives Indian developers and startups more scope to build for their own, and enterprise needs.”

Under the new arrangement, both the processing of an API request and the model computation that generates its response will take place in India for supported workloads. Supported customer content will also be stored in the country, the company said.

The launch covers direct API usage and currently supports GPT-6 Luna input and output through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs. Customers can access the capability by creating a new API project, selecting India for both storage and processing, and using the corresponding India regional endpoint.

The development comes as OpenAI expands its presence in India. Earlier this year, the company introduced OpenAI for India, an initiative spanning AI infrastructure, enterprise adoption, skills development and local partnerships. The initiative included a partnership with Tata Group to develop domestic AI data-centre capacity, according to OpenAI.

OpenAI models were also made available for in-country inference through Amazon Web Services’ Bedrock platform. AWS announced the availability of OpenAI models on Bedrock in August 2026, including regional inference capabilities for supported models.

OpenAI said its now launched API inference residency offering is available in other parts of the world, with India, Australia and Japan among the latest markets to receive the capability.

articles.title: Six researchers win Infosys Science Foundation prizes for 2026
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A total of 222 applications were received across six categories with the highest for ‘Engineering and Computer Science’ category, ISF said

The Infosys Science Foundation (ISF) on Thursday (November 12, 2026) announced the winners of the ‘Infosys Prize 2026’ in six categories — Economics, Engineering and Computer Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, Life Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, and Physical Sciences.
Among the recipients is Riddhipratim Basu, Associate Professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (ICTS-TIFR) in Bengaluru.

The prize for each category comprises a gold medal, a citation, and a prize purse of $100,000 (or its equivalent in Indian rupees). The laureates of Infosys Prize 2026 were selected by an international panel of jurors comprising renowned scholars and experts.

This year 222 applications were received compared to 150 last year, ISF Trustee Kris Gopalakrishnan said. He added that the highest number of applications were received in the Engineering and Computer Science category and the youngest winner this year is 31 years of age.

ISF said that from 2024, the prize has shifted focus to honour researchers under the age of 40, emphasising the need for early recognition of exceptional talent. “This encouragement of early career researchers will serve as an inspiration for the next generation of scholars and future innovators,” it said.

“Recognising exceptional researchers early in their careers is particularly important, as it gives them the encouragement and opportunity to pursue bold questions, challenge established thinking and make lasting contributions to their fields,” ISF President Srinath Batni said.
Karthik Sastry, Associate Professor of Economics and Public Affairs | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Karthik Sastry, Associate Professor of Economics and Public Affairs at Princeton University, has won the award for his contributions to the field of climate change, and technological innovation, and to the study of business cycle fluctuations. “His work provides deep insights into how societies adapt to climate change through technological innovations and is likely to have far-reaching policy implications,” the jury said.
Swarun Kumar, Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Swarun Kumar, Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University, has been awarded in this category for his pioneering work that extends low-power wireless networks beyond information delivery to perception and action in the physical world. He combines insights on the physics of wireless technology with novel architectures and algorithms to obtain innovative designs in connectivity, sensing, control, and actuation.

articles.title: T.N. BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran alleges Keralam medical waste dumped in Tenkasi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP leader urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to take up the issue with his Keralam counterpart

BJP Tamil Nadu unit president Nainar Nagenthran on Thursday (November 12, 2026) alleged that hazardous medical waste brought from the neighbouring State of Keralam was being dumped and burnt in agricultural lands and open spaces in Tenkasi district. He also charged that the TVK-led government in Tamil Nadu had failed to prevent it.

In a social media post, Mr. Nagenthran said bottles bearing labels indicating that they were meant for sale only in Keralam, along with hazardous waste, were found dumped in Tenkasi district, and that Tamil Nadu authorities had failed to effectively monitor border check-posts.

Alleging that the problem extended beyond Tenkasi to other border districts of the State, Mr. Nagenthran said the dumping of Keralam’s waste was contaminating Tamil Nadu’s agricultural lands and posing a threat to public health.

The BJP leader urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to take up the issue with his Keralam counterpart, strengthen surveillance at border check-posts, seize vehicles transporting waste illegally, and invoke the Goondas Act against those involved.

articles.title: Activist demands immediate monitoring of BJP-SP social media war in U.P. ahead of Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Activist Amitabh Thakur adds that his political party, Azad Adhikar Sena, will independently monitor social media content and initiate complaints and action against unlawful propaganda

Lucknow-based social activist Amitabh Thakur wrote a letter to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) on Thursday (November 12, 2026), expressing serious concern over the increasingly aggressive and personal nature of the social-media war between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly Elections in 2027.

In his letter to the Election Commission of India (ECI), Mr. Thakur sought immediate monitoring and stringent legal action over personal attacks, abusive remarks, AI-generated or manipulated videos, and misleading propaganda and messages that exploit communal sensitivities, which are posing serious challenges to public morality, democratic norms, social harmony, and law and order.

“I observed that personal attacks, abusive remarks, AI-generated or manipulated videos, misleading propaganda and messages exploiting communal sensitivities are posing serious challenges to public morality, democratic norms, social harmony and law and order during election time. I urged the authorities to establish dedicated social media monitoring cells immediately, without waiting for the announcement of elections or enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct, and to ensure prompt and stringent action against unlawful content,” he told The Hindu , over the phone.
Mr. Thakur added that his political party, Azad Adhikar Sena, will independently monitor social media content and initiate complaints and action against unlawful propaganda

articles.title: Minor fire at Srikalahasti temple kitchen contained, no major damage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kitchen staff tried to bring the fire under control, but when it began to go beyond their ability to manage, the panicked workers rushed out of the building, thereby averting a mishap
A minor fire was reported in the kitchen attached to the famed Srikalahastheeswara Swamy temple in Srikalahasti town of Tirupati district on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The fire accident was attributed to an electrical short circuit, which aggravated when the ghee kept for making the “Prasadam,” meant to be offered to the deity before distribution to the public, caught fire from the stove and spread to the entire hall.
The kitchen staff tried to bring the fire under control, but when it began to go beyond their ability to manage, the panicked workers rushed out of the building, thereby averting a mishap.
After the temple staff initially tried to tame the flames with the fire safety equipment on hand, fire personnel stepped in promptly and brought the raging fire under control.
The queue line was closed, and devotees were barred from entering the temple premises until the fire was extinguished.
No major damage was reported from this incident, said the temple’s executive officer, B. K. Venkatesulu.

articles.title: Two lose nearly ₹1 crore in separate online trading frauds in Keralam’s Kozhikode
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Preliminary investigations revealed that the duped funds were systematically routed through multiple mule bank accounts and current accounts rented specifically for the operation by the accused

articles.title: Kejriwal, his daughter get death threat from ‘Bishnoi gang member’; case filed in Punjab
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi AAP MLA Jarnail Singh alleged caller demanded ₹7 crore from Mr. Kejriwal and threatened to kill him and his daughter Harshita Kejriwal if the money was not paid

The Punjab Police has registered a case following a complaint filed by Delhi AAP MLA Jarnail Singh, who claimed to have received a death threat message concerning party leader Arvind Kejriwal and his daughter, along with a demand for ₹7 crore.
The MLA lodged his complaint with the Mohali police, which registered a case under relevant sections of the BNS and the Information and Technology Act.

In his complaint to the Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police, Tilak Nagar MLA Singh claimed that he received both a call and a WhatsApp message on his mobile phone on November 6 from an individual, claiming to be a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.
The alleged caller demanded ₹7 crore from Mr. Kejriwal and threatened to kill him and his daughter Harshita Kejriwal if the money was not paid, according to the complaint filed by the AAP MLA.

In his complaint, which is part of the FIR, Mr. Singh claimed that the caller stated, "Lawrence Bishnoi gang se bol raha hun, Arvind Kejriwal ko bol de, 7 crore de do nahin to Arvind Kejriwal or uski ladki Harshita Kejriwal ko jaan se maar dunga." (I am speaking from the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. Tell Arvind Kejriwal that if he does not pay Rs 7 crore, then I will kill both him and his daughter.)
ALSO WATCH Tiger Shroff shooting: Is Lawrence Bishnoi the new Bollywood don? | Insight India

"Given his stature as a high-profile figure, the threat has caused national and public security risks. The sender has unlawfully used my position as an elected representative to channel extortionist demands and death threats directed at Arvind Kejriwal and his family. The acts committed by the sender constitute serious offences," Mr. Singh wrote in his complaint.

The Delhi MLA also requested a comprehensive investigation and to trace the CDRs, IP logs and location of the device to arrest the culprit before anything untoward happens. Necessary coordination with relevant law enforcement and security authorities should also be initiated to ensure full protection for the targeted individuals, he said.

Following the complaint, the Mohali police registered a case under relevant sections including 308 (4) (extortion), 351 (2) (criminal intimidation), 351 (4) (criminal intimidation by anonymous communication, 111 (2) (organised crime) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the relevant section of the IT Act at the Cyber Crime Police Station in Mohali.

articles.title: DRDL Director highlights importance of indigenous research
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Signing an MoU with Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education, Ankathi Raju urges students and faculty to actively take up research activities, innovation and technology development to contribute towards national missions

Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education Deemed-to-be-University, Vijayawada, has inked a pact with the Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL), Hyderabad, on Thursday to provide opportunities for academic interaction, research engagement and knowledge sharing.
The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between DRDL Director Ankathi Raju and Siddhartha University Vice-Chancellor P. Venkateswara Rao.

Speaking about the contributions made by the DRDL to the country’s defence research and technological advancement, Mr. Ankathi Raju said the DRDL plays a crucial role in the design and development of advanced missile systems and strategic defence technologies, including aerodynamics, propulsion systems, navigation, guidance, control systems and other indigenous technologies that strengthen India’s national security and self-reliance.

He highlighted the importance of indigenous research, technological innovation and collaboration between premier research organisations and academic institutions and urged students and faculty to actively take up research activities, innovation and technology development to contribute towards national missions.
The programme was attended by the deans of all schools, heads of various departments and representatives of different academic and administrative units of the university.

Signing an MoU with Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education, Ankathi Raju urges students and faculty to actively take up research activities, innovation and technology development to contribute towards national missions

Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education Deemed-to-be-University, Vijayawada, has inked a pact with the Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL), Hyderabad, on Thursday to provide opportunities for academic interaction, research engagement and knowledge sharing.

The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between DRDL Director Ankathi Raju and Siddhartha University Vice-Chancellor P. Venkateswara Rao.

Speaking about the contributions made by the DRDL to the country’s defence research and technological advancement, Mr. Ankathi Raju said the DRDL plays a crucial role in the design and development of advanced missile systems and strategic defence technologies, including aerodynamics, propulsion systems, navigation, guidance, control systems and other indigenous technologies that strengthen India’s national security and self-reliance.

He highlighted the importance of indigenous research, technological innovation and collaboration between premier research organisations and academic institutions and urged students and faculty to actively take up research activities, innovation and technology development to contribute towards national missions.

The programme was attended by the deans of all schools, heads of various departments and representatives of different academic and administrative units of the university.

articles.title: CPI seeks probe into ‘poll discrepancies’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ramakrishna demands resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of favouring BJP and RSS

The Communist Party of India (CPI) has demanded a comprehensive probe by the Union government into alleged discrepancies between votes polled and counted in the Lok Sabha elections, as highlighted by investigative journalism organisation, The Reporters' Collective.

Addressing the media at Dasari Bhavan here on Thursday, CPI national secretary K. Ramakrishna and State secretary Gujjula Eswaraiah alleged that the findings raised serious questions about the integrity of the electoral process.

Mr. Ramakrishna said the organisation had analysed data from around 530 Lok Sabha constituencies and reported discrepancies in Maharashtra, Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir. He demanded that the Election Commission of India's internal reports be made public and subjected to scrutiny.

Mr. Ramakrishna demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of favouring the BJP and the RSS. He questioned the addition of 50 to 60 million voters ahead of the Maharashtra Assembly elections, despite the BJP's setback in the preceding parliamentary elections.

He said the CPI national executive would meet in New Delhi on November 16 and 17 to discuss organising a nationwide movement along with INDIA bloc partners, mass organisations and civil rights groups.

Mr. Eswaraiah said victories secured unanimously in several rural and urban local bodies could not be celebrated if they were allegedly achieved through administrative pressure. Free elections and genuine voter participation were essential for democratic legitimacy, he said.
He announced a State-wide agitation against the proposed privatisation, warning that the decision would invite public opposition.

The CPI leaders criticised the Centre and the State government for “failing to provide adequate relief to farmers and people affected by drought and successive cyclones”. They said several villages continued to face power outages even 14 to 15 days after the cyclones made landfall.

They expressed concern over rising prices of rice, pulses, tomatoes, onions, garlic and ginger, alleging that the governments had failed to intervene effectively in the market. CPI State Secretariat member Donepudi Shankar was also present.

articles.title: Medical examination of recaptured prisoners, allegedly thrashed by Theni jail warders, confirms injuries
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan of the Madras High Court direct government doctors to provide medical treatment to the injured prisoners

A medical examination ordered by the Madras High Court with respect to four out of 17 recaptured prisoners, who escaped from Theni district jail on October 26, 2026, and allegedly thrashed by the warders after their recapture within two days, has revealed that they are suffering from multiple injuries.

A Division Bench of Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan were told that the medical examination of three prisoners, now shifted to the Salem central prison, and the fourth prisoner lodged at Palayamkottai central prison, by government doctors had confirmed the injuries sustained by them.

The judges decided to take a further call on the issue after receipt of a report from the Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority (TNSLSA) on the inquiry that it had initiated with respect to allegations of the 17 prisoners having escaped from the prison only because of torture and ill-treatment by the warders.

They directed the High Court Registry to list a writ petition filed by K. Arumugathammal, mother of two of the prisoners, on November 17, 2026, since the TNSLSA report was expected to be submitted to its executive chairman Justice S.M. Subramaniam, the seniormost judge of the High Court, only by November 16, 2026.

In the meantime, the Deans of Government Mohan Kumaramangalam Medical College Hospital in Salem and the Government Medical College Hospital in Tirunelveli were directed to provide requisite medical treatment to the injured prisoners and the prison authorities were directed to extend full cooperation to the doctors.

The Division Bench also directed the chairpersons of the district legal services authority in Salem and Tirunelveli to monitor the medical treatment provided to the injured prisoners until it could hear the writ petition next on November 17, 2026, and pass further orders.

The writ petitioner had filed the case accusing the Theni prison warders of having beaten all 17 recaptured prisoners, including her sons K. Meenakshi Sundaram (26) and K. Tirupathi (22), black and blue before transferring them to various other prisons spread across the State.

The petitioner said that one of her sons had been transferred to Salem central prison and the other to Palayamkottai and that their co-prisoners N. Solai Mugileswaran (19) and P. Sabarinathan (24) were also suffering from injuries sustained due to the thrashing by the warders after their recapture.

Passing interim orders in her case on November 3, 2026, the Division Bench led by Justice Chandira had ordered constitution of two medical teams comprising government doctors to examine the four inmates in the Salem and Palayamkottai prisons and file their reports before the court.

articles.title: Vizag CII Summit: ReNew to invest ₹80,000 crore in green data centre, solar manufacturing in Andhra Pradesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Investments include a ₹67,000-crore Green Hyperscale Data Centre in Anakapalli, ₹11,000-crore polysilicon and metallurgical silicon manufacturing facilities in Anakapalli and Nellore; and ₹1,500-crore permanent magnet manufacturing facility in Rambilli

ReNew Energy Global Plc, a leading decarbonisation solutions company, has announced fresh investments of approximately ₹80,000 crore in Andhra Pradesh, spanning digital infrastructure and clean energy manufacturing.

The investments include a ₹67,000-crore 1 GW Green Hyperscale Data Centre in Anakapalli, ₹11,000-crore polysilicon and metallurgical silicon manufacturing facilities in Anakapalli and Nellore; and a ₹1,500-crore permanent magnet manufacturing facility in Rambilli.
Besides, the company will set up the ReNew Centre for Technical Excellence in Visakhapatnam under the PM SETU Scheme.
The announcements were made at the CII Partnership Summit 2026 held in Visakhapatnam under the leadership of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, and in the presence of IT & HRD Minister Nara Lokesh.
Together, the investments expand ReNew’s presence across digital infrastructure, renewable energy, clean energy manufacturing and skilling, deepening its long-term partnership with Andhra Pradesh.

Commenting on the proposals, Sumant Sinha, Founder-Chairman and CEO of ReNew, said that Andhra Pradesh was emerging as an important destination for India’s industrial and digital growth, and ReNew’s investments would bring together two of India’s biggest growth opportunities, digitalisation and decarbonisation, while strengthening clean energy manufacturing, infrastructure and skills.

ReNew was working in tandem with the Andhra Pradesh government towards achieving the State’s target of generating 78.50 GW of solar, 35 GW of wind power capacity, and 25 GWh of battery energy storage systems, Mr. Sinha said.
Company’s co-founder Vaishali Nigam Sinha and CEO (Solar Manufacturing) Sanjay Varghese were present.

articles.title: India records 38% drop in TB mortality since 2015: WHO report
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: World Health Organization’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 showed a total of 1.13 million people died from tuberculosis last year

India has seen a 38% reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality since 2015, compared to a global average of 35%, and a 94% treatment success rate among patients with drug-susceptible TB, according to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026.
Last year, the South-East Asia Region recorded the largest number of new TB cases (35%), followed by the Western Pacific Region (27%) and the African Region (25%).

Around 88% of new TB cases occurred in 30 countries. India (about a quarter), Indonesia (10%), the Philippines (6.8%), China (6.5%), Pakistan (6.4%), Nigeria (4.9%), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (3.9%) and Bangladesh (3.7%) accounted for about a q of the global total.

Globally, about 50% of people treated for TB and their households face total costs (direct medical expenditures, non-medical expenditures, and indirect costs such as income losses) that are catastrophic (greater than 20% of total household income).

People with compromised immune systems, such as those living with HIV, undernutrition or diabetes, or people who use tobacco have a higher risk of falling ill. An estimated 9.6 lakh new TB cases were attributable to undernutrition, 9.2 lakh to diabetes, 7.3 lakh to alcohol use disorders, 6.9 lakh to smoking and 5.5 lakh to HIV infection.

The report showed a total of 1.13 million people died from TB in 2025. Globally, TB is the world’s leading cause of death from a single infectious agent. Last year, an estimated 10.6 million people fell ill with TB worldwide, including 5.7 million men, 3.7 million women and 1.2 million children.

Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) remains a public health crisis and a health security threat. Only about two in five people with drug-resistant TB received treatment in 2025. Global efforts to combat TB have saved an estimated 86 million lives since 2000.
Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by bacteria that most often affects the lungs. It spreads through the air when people with TB cough, sneeze or spit. TB is preventable and curable.
Between December 7, 2024 and November 8, 2026, the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan achieved significant progress, identifying and bringing over 25 crore individuals within the scope of screening activities.

“India’s reduction in TB mortality has been the result of interventions under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), including proactive case finding including use of AI-enabled X-rays, rapid diagnostics, prompt treatment initiation, differentiated TB care, and nutritional support through the Nikshay Poshan Yojana and Nikshay Mitra initiative. World Health Organization’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 showed a total of 1.13 million people died from tuberculosis last year

India has seen a 38% reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality since 2015, compared to a global average of 35%, and a 94% treatment success rate among patients with drug-susceptible TB, according to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026.

Last year, the South-East Asia Region recorded the largest number of new TB cases (35%), followed by the Western Pacific Region (27%) and the African Region (25%).

Around 88% of new TB cases occurred in 30 countries. India (about a quarter), Indonesia (10%), the Philippines (6.8%), China (6.5%), Pakistan (6.4%), Nigeria (4.9%), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (3.9%) and Bangladesh (3.7%) accounted for about a q of the global total.

Globally, about 50% of people treated for TB and their households face total costs (direct medical expenditures, non-medical expenditures, and indirect costs such as income losses) that are catastrophic (greater than 20% of total household income).

People with compromised immune systems, such as those living with HIV, undernutrition or diabetes, or people who use tobacco have a higher risk of falling ill. An estimated 9.6 lakh new TB cases were attributable to undernutrition, 9.2 lakh to diabetes, 7.3 lakh to alcohol use disorders, 6.9 lakh to smoking and 5.5 lakh to HIV infection.

The report showed a total of 1.13 million people died from TB in 2025. Globally, TB is the world’s leading cause of death from a single infectious agent. Last year, an estimated 10.6 million people fell ill with TB worldwide, including 5.7 million men, 3.7 million women and 1.2 million children.

Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) remains a public health crisis and a health security threat. Only about two in five people with drug-resistant TB received treatment in 2025. Global efforts to combat TB have saved an estimated 86 million lives since 2000.

Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by bacteria that most often affects the lungs. It spreads through the air when people with TB cough, sneeze or spit. TB is preventable and curable.

Between December 7, 2024 and November 8, 2026, the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan achieved significant progress, identifying and bringing over 25 crore individuals within the scope of screening activities.

“India’s reduction in TB mortality has been the result of interventions under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), including proactive case finding including use of AI-enabled X-rays, rapid diagnostics, prompt treatment initiation, differentiated TB care, and nutritional support through the Nikshay Poshan Yojana and Nikshay Mitra initiative. These interventions were supported by AI tools for identification of hotspots, prediction of high-risk TB cases prone for adverse outcomes, Khushi – AI Chatbot & Avatar Videobot, etc.,” the Union Health Ministry statement said.

articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Officials stated that DISCOMs would be evaluated for their performance over a five-year period, following by transmission, generation, renewable energy and RDSS.

The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas.

The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development.

Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise.
The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27.
Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups..
“We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said.
The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply.

Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions.
“Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.

The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.

articles.title: Retail inflation crosses RBI’s upper limit for first time in two years, comes in at 6.1% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The Consumer Price Index saw almost all categories hit series highs as inflation spread across sectors of the economy

Retail inflation rose to 6.1% in October 2026, crossing the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) upper threshold for the first time in two years. The continued uptick in inflation, while driven by food and fuel prices, has now spread to nearly all sectors, data released by the government on Thursday shows.

The RBI targets an inflation rate of 4% with a comfort band of 2% higher or lower than figure. Inflation as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) last crossed this upper threshold of 6% in October 2024, when it came in at 6.2%. Retail inflation in October 2026 was the highest since then.

The new series of the CPI, with a base year of 2024, has sectoral data that goes back to only January 2026, which means a historical analysis is possible only up to that point. Within that, the latest data shows inflation across most categories rose to series highs in October 2026.

“Although inflation remains predominantly supply-driven, stronger consumer demand pull associated with festive-season purchases may have added to price pressures, reinforcing the RBI’s decision to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%,” Pranjal Ghate, economist at Brickwork Ratings said, referring to the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) latest decision in early October 2026.

The data shows that inflation in the food and beverages category rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026, the highest in the series. Coupled with this, rising fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose to 5.8% in October, a series high.

As a result of accelerating food and transport prices, inflation in the restaurant and accommodation services category jumped to 10.1% in October, the first time it has come in at double-digits in the new series.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, some food prices could rise further in the coming months.

“The ongoing harvest prospects will throw more light on how food prices behave,” Mr. Sabnavis said. “Area under cultivation was lower for rice, maize, oilseeds, cotton and sugarcane. It has also been reported that pulses production, especially tur, could be lower this time, which can lead to a spike in prices.”
Apart from food and fuel, the data shows that other aspects of day-to-day life have also seen prices rising at a faster pace.

Clothing and footwear, for example, saw inflation coming in at nearly 5% in October 2026 — the highest in this series — from 3.9% in the previous month. The ‘furnishings, household equipment, and routine household maintenance’ category saw inflation quicken to 3.9% in October, also a series high.
