articles.title: Andhra Pradesh to spend Rs.632 crore on restoration of 789 lift irrigation schemes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The restored schemes will provide irrigation to 7.49 lakh acres, officials tell Chief Minister Naidu

The Andhra Pradesh government will spend ₹632.07 crore on restoring 789 defunct lift irrigation schemes across the State, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said, directing officials to complete all repairs by June 2027 to ensure their availability for the ensuing kharif season.

Reviewing irrigation projects and lift irrigation schemes at his camp office on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), Mr. Naidu instructed officials to undertake field inspections, call tenders immediately and commence repair works without delay. He said all 789 schemes identified for restoration must be made operational before the commencement of the agricultural season.

Officials informed the Chief Minister that the restoration works would require ₹632.07 crore and help provide irrigation facilities to 7.49 lakh acres. Mr. Naidu directed the Water Resources Department to establish a robust mechanism for the operation and maintenance of the schemes.

He asked the Jalaharathi Corporation to take up continuous monitoring of the lift irrigation schemes by setting up a dedicated division. If necessary, a Chief Engineer or Superintending Engineer should be appointed for each district to oversee their functioning and maintenance, he said.

The officials informed the Chief Minister that 4,061 acres had been identified out of 5,565 acres available with the Water Resources Department for setting up solar power plants. These installations could generate 877.3 MW of electricity.

The restored schemes will provide irrigation to 7.49 lakh acres, officials tell Chief Minister Naidu

The Andhra Pradesh government will spend ₹632.07 crore on restoring 789 defunct lift irrigation schemes across the State, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said, directing officials to complete all repairs by June 2027 to ensure their availability for the ensuing kharif season.

Reviewing irrigation projects and lift irrigation schemes at his camp office on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), Mr. Naidu instructed officials to undertake field inspections, call tenders immediately and commence repair works without delay. He said all 789 schemes identified for restoration must be made operational before the commencement of the agricultural season.

Officials informed the Chief Minister that the restoration works would require ₹632.07 crore and help provide irrigation facilities to 7.49 lakh acres. Mr. Naidu directed the Water Resources Department to establish a robust mechanism for the operation and maintenance of the schemes.

He asked the Jalaharathi Corporation to take up continuous monitoring of the lift irrigation schemes by setting up a dedicated division. If necessary, a Chief Engineer or Superintending Engineer should be appointed for each district to oversee their functioning and maintenance, he said.

The officials informed the Chief Minister that 4,061 acres had been identified out of 5,565 acres available with the Water Resources Department for setting up solar power plants. These installations could generate 877.3 MW of electricity.

In addition, 110 acres across 84 locations under the Irrigation Development Corporation could be utilised for solar power generation, with a potential capacity of 25.8 MW.

In all, 4,171 acres could be utilised to establish solar power plants with a combined generation capacity of 903.1 MW.

Mr. Naidu suggested exploring the possibilities of generating solar and hydropower by utilising canal infrastructure as well. He asked officials to prepare a plan to ensure uninterrupted power supply to lift irrigation schemes during the agricultural season and examine the possibility of selling surplus electricity to the grid to generate revenue.

fullParagraphs: The controversy caused a furore in Tamil Nadu, as the case heads into a Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption inquiry, court intervention and the scope of investigations has now explanded to include inventories in several other libraries

The story so far: A veritable pandora’s box of literary and political controversy was opened on November 6, 2026, when Sahitya Akademi winner Perumal Murugan wrote about several irregularities in the procurement of books for the newly-inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore. He wrote, and later spoke online, about how thousands of exorbitantly-priced books had been procured for the library with questionable authorship, full of factual errors and were seemingly AI generated. He also pointed out that these books had been procured at inflated rates, many times higher than current market rates for similar publications.

It has since caused a furore in Tamil Nadu, as the case heads into a Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption inquiry, court intervention and the scope of investigations has now explanded to include inventories in several other libraries, and it has also started an intense political blame game with the prime actors being the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and its predecessor, now in the Opposition, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam.

articles.title: Congress launches ‘Punjab Mangda Insaaf’ campaign ahead of State polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh and Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the State Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa launched the campaign at the party headquarters in Chandigarh
The Punjab Congress on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) rolled out 'Punjab Mangda Insaaf' campaign to reach out to every section of society and raise their concerns effectively ahead of the State polls.
Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh and Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the State Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa launched the campaign at the party headquarters in Chandigarh.
'Punjab Mangda Insaaf' is aimed at connecting with the people of Punjab and raising issues concerning farmers, youths, drugs, law and order and other public concerns, according to the party.
Speaking to reporters in Chandigarh, LoP Bajwa said that under this campaign, the Punjab Congress leadership will visit different parts of Punjab and raise issues concerning all sections of society.

"We will speak about the fraud with government employees and pensioners by the AAP government, the old pension scheme not being implemented, the law and order situation and the poor financial health of the State," he said.
Mr. Bajwa claimed the AAP government has failed on all fronts.

"AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal had promised Rs 54,000 crore funds per annum for setting up colleges, medical colleges, new infrastructure including roads, bridges. Not even a single penny was given. We will ask Kejriwal where that money has gone," he said.
"They did nothing for farmers, women or traders," he claimed.
Asked about Congress MP Charanjit Singh Channi's cycle yatra, which will commence on November 12, Mr. Bajwa said it is also part of the party's programme.
"Channi saab is our brother. With his programme, the message of the Congress will reach Punjab. We will do it together. We all will go there [cycle yatra] tomorrow as well," he said.

articles.title: God belongs to everyone, says Akhilesh on his Ayodhya visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Claiming the BJP wins elections through dishonesty and fraud, the SP chief said that voters have made up their mind to bring his party to power in U.P.; he called for a voter list to be linked to Aadhaar

Dismissing the BJP’s criticism of his plans to visit Ayodhya next month, Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) emphasised that “God belongs to everyone” and slammed his critics for their alleged loot and destruction in Ayodhya.
Mr. Yadav is scheduled to visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on December 12, with his family. BJP leaders triggered a political war of words by terming his visit politically motivated.

Samajwadi Party National president Akhilesh Yadav celebrates the birthday of Khajanchi, the child who was born in a bank queue during demonetisation, by presenting him with gifts and cash during a press conference at the party office in Lucknow. | Photo Credit: ANI

“God belongs to everyone. So why should we not visit these places? We will visit Kedareshwar, Mathura and Vrindavan as well. We have been visiting these places before, and we will continue to do so. Those who looted and destroyed the livelihood of common people should answer,” Mr. Yadav told journalists in Lucknow.
The SP president claimed that Uttar Pradesh voters have determined to bring his party back into power in the State.

“The farmers, youth, labourers, and traders of Uttar Pradesh want change. The public has made up its mind to form the government of the Samajwadi Party in 2027. The people of the State are ready; the end of the BJP is near. Under the BJP government, injustice, oppression, inflation, and unemployment are at their peak. The Chief Minister is unaware of the employment rate and unemployment rate,” Mr. Yadav said, urging party workers to win booths and be vigilant.

“The BJP wins elections through dishonesty and fraud. The BJP wanted to commit dishonesty through the [special intensive revision] SIR process, but the workers of the Samajwadi Party and the PDA guards saved their votes. It is the responsibility of all leaders and workers to keep their votes safe and strengthen the booths,” he added.

The SP chief demanded that the voter list be linked with Aadhaar cards and said that these cards should be made of metal so that fakes cannot be created. “If everyone’s Aadhaar card is biometric, then why is the voter list not being linked to the Aadhaar card? When discussions are being held about Digital India and becoming equal to the world, why is the voter list not being linked to the Aadhaar card?” he asked.

Mr. Yadav claimed that the BJP was scared of the PDA, his acronym for an alliance of minorities, Dalits, and backward class voters. “Now the fight is not 80 versus 20, but 95 versus 5. This time in the Assembly elections, the BJP will not be visible on the ground. Seeing the BJP’s defeat, the Chief Minister’s language and behaviour have changed,” he said.
Celebrating the birthday of Khajanchi, a 10-year-old boy born during demonetisation in 2016, Mr. Yadav described ‘note bandi ’ as the most corrupt decision in the world’s history.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ms. Indira Dewri has renewed her demand for a fresh CBI probe and DNA test to establish the paternity of her 23-year-old son
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has backed a woman’s demand for justice in a 23-year-old paternity row involving former Uttarakhand Minister and Congress leader Harak Singh Rawat.
In a social media post on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), the Chief Minister said he had met Ms. Indira Dewri, also known as Jenny, who claims that Mr. Rawat raped and impregnated her in 2003.

Condemning the treatment Ms. Dewri — who hails from Sadiya in Assam’s Tinsukia district — had received, Mr. Sarma wrote: “Yesterday (November 10, 2026), I met Jenny, a resident of Assam. What a man named Harak Singh Rawat from Uttarakhand did to her is extremely wrong and reprehensible. No one should have to suffer the kind of cruelty she endured. I stand firmly with her in this fight for justice.”
In the meeting, Ms. Dewri renewed her demand for a DNA test and a fresh Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe to establish the paternity of her 23-year-old son.
She told journalists in Dehradun on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) that she has appealed to Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami for justice.
She would stay in Dehradun until her demands were addressed, she said.
Ms. Dewri criticised the earlier CBI investigation, alleging the agency had not recorded her statement properly. She also said the CBI did not collect samples from her son for a DNA test.
“I have received threats. I need protection,” she said, while also insisting on a narco-analysis.
Mr. Rawat denied the allegations, including the charge of rape, and challenged those involved to undergo DNA tests under court supervision.
He accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of reviving the controversy to target him and the Congress party ahead of State Assembly elections slated for 2027.

articles.title: Mamata skips Bhai Phonta celebrations; her brother joins rebel camp, praises Suvendu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While some of the former CM’s supporters gathered at her residence, most of her erstwhile loyalists were conspicuous by their absence

Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) skipped the Bhai Phonta festivities at her residence, breaking a tradition going back several years when leaders of her party would make a beeline to seek her blessing.

Celebrated as Bhai Dooj in other parts of India, sisters apply a tika on their brothers’ foreheads as a mark of love, and pray for their long and healthy lives. Ms. Banerjee, who is also called ‘ Didi’ (elder sister), would offer the tilak to a number of her party leaders and supporters.

“Mamata di is not observing Bhai Phonta. She did not observe Bijoya [Vijayadasami] before. She will not observe Bhai Phonta this time either. In light of the attacks, terror, police brutality and arrests on false charges that TMC [Trinamool Congress] workers have faced since the elections, @MamataOfficial did not observe Bijoya this time,” Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) spokesperson Kunal Ghosh said.

“Since the family’s Kali Puja could not be cancelled, Ms. Banerjee performed the puja for the goddess. But she will not hold any Bhai Phonta ceremony. Anyone may come to see her. But Didi will not hold a Bhai Phonta ceremony this time,” Mr. Ghosh said.

While some of Ms. Banerjee’s supporters gathered at her residence, most of her erstwhile loyalists, who have since deserted her, were conspicuous by their absence. articles.title: CM Vijay urges TVK MLAs to stay united, prioritise public grievances, avoid controversies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: His meeting with the party MLAs assumes significance against the backdrop of his government completing six months in office and some legislators recently getting involved in controversies

Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) held a meeting with his party MLAs for nearly three hours at a private resort near Mamallapuram in Chengalpattu district and urged them to stay united, work for the people and refrain from getting involved in controversies.

His meeting with the party MLAs assumes significance against the backdrop of his government completing six months in office and some legislators recently getting involved in controversies. Barring a few legislators, the majority of the legislators participated in the meeting.

Sources who attended the meeting told The Hindu that Mr. Vijay interacted with the MLAs in batches of 10, spending nearly 10 to 15 minutes with each batch. He first held discussions with the women MLAs of the party. Later, he interacted with the other MLAs and finally with the Ministers.

Sources said Mr. Vijay conveyed Deepavali greetings to the MLAs and distributed saris and dhotis to them. Some MLAs were learnt to have raised the issue of not being able to meet him frequently and of non-cooperation from officials. The Chief Minister took note of their concerns and told them to bring forward grievances from their respective Assembly constituencies and meet him at the Secretariat.

He also urged the party MLAs to stay united and refrain from getting involved in any controversies. He is also learnt to have told them that the Opposition parties might attempt to create controversies and cautioned them to remain vigilant.

articles.title: Amid call for Ladakh protest, CEO prohibits dharnas in Leh, Kargil over upcoming polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The order came a day after Ladakh’s civil society groups announced that agitations to push a slew of demands would resume on November 12

With Ladakh’s civil society groups threatening to resume agitations to push a slew of demands, the Union Territory’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) issued an order prohibiting all dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins and rallies within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil while the Model Code of Conduct is in force ahead of local body elections.
The order said the restrictions will remain in force until the completion of the election process for the municipal committees of Leh and Kargil this month.

“The Model Code requires maintenance of an atmosphere conducive to free, fair and peaceful elections, and no activity should be permitted which may create intimidation, fear or undue influence among electors,” said the order.

It said organising political dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies, or similar collective activities during this period would have the potential to intimidate voters, disturb public order, and vitiate the atmosphere for free and fair elections.

It directed all political parties, candidates, and their agents to strictly adhere to the provisions of the Model Code of Conduct and ensure no activity is undertaken that may intimidate, coerce, or unduly influence electors.
The District Election Officers, or Deputy Commissioners, of Leh and Kargil and the Superintendents of Police of the districts were directed “to ensure strict compliance of the order”.
“Any violation will be dealt with firmly in accordance with law, including proceedings under relevant provisions and the Model Code of Conduct,” it added.

The order came a day after Leh Apex Body (LAB) called for an agitation, with a sit-in from November 12, to press their demands on a slew of issues, including the resumption of talks between the Centre and Ladakh bodies, making public the status of the judicial inquiry report into the September 24, 2025, violence that left four people dead, and the postponement of hill council elections till next year.

Members of the LAB, including co-chairman Tsering Dorjey Lakrook and activist Sonam Wangchuk, on Wednesday made a video appeal to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi “to intervene before people of Ladakh are forced to start peaceful but intense agitations to demonstrate our pain”.

“While the judicial inquiry commission report on the September 24 incidents in Leh moves at a snail’s pace even after a year of the incident, and the talks on restoration of democracy have broken down, the U.T. administration is moving at rocket speed to conduct some kind of council elections here, apparently to have people of their choice installed to negotiate on democracy and safeguards here,” said Mr. Wancghuk.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

The order came a day after Ladakh’s civil society groups announced that agitations to push a slew of demands would resume on November 12

With Ladakh’s civil society groups threatening to resume agitations to push a slew of demands, the Union Territory’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) issued an order prohibiting all dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins and rallies within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil while the Model Code of Conduct is in force ahead of local body elections.

The order said the restrictions will remain in force until the completion of the election process for the municipal committees of Leh and Kargil this month.

“The Model Code requires maintenance of an atmosphere conducive to free, fair and peaceful elections, and no activity should be permitted which may create intimidation, fear or undue influence among electors,” said the order.

It said organising political dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies, or similar collective activities during this period would have the potential to intimidate voters, disturb public order, and vitiate the atmosphere for free and fair elections.

It directed all political parties, candidates, and their agents to strictly adhere to the provisions of the Model Code of Conduct and ensure no activity is undertaken that may intimidate, coerce, or unduly influence electors.

The District Election Officers, or Deputy Commissioners, of Leh and Kargil and the Superintendents of Police of the districts were directed “to ensure strict compliance of the order”.

“Any violation will be dealt with firmly in accordance with law, including proceedings under relevant provisions and the Model Code of Conduct,” it added.

The order came a day after Leh Apex Body (LAB) called for an agitation, with a sit-in from November 12, to press their demands on a slew of issues, including the resumption of talks between the Centre and Ladakh bodies, making public the status of the judicial inquiry report into the September 24, 2025, violence that left four people dead, and the postponement of hill council elections till next year.

Members of the LAB, including co-chairman Tsering Dorjey Lakrook and activist Sonam Wangchuk, on Wednesday made a video appeal to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi “to intervene before people of Ladakh are forced to start peaceful but intense agitations to demonstrate our pain”.

“While the judicial inquiry commission report on the September 24 incidents in Leh moves at a snail’s pace even after a year of the incident, and the talks on restoration of democracy have broken down, the U.T. administration is moving at rocket speed to conduct some kind of council elections here, apparently to have people of their choice installed to negotiate on democracy and safeguards here,” said Mr. Wancghuk.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “While the judicial inquiry commission report on the September 24 incidents in Leh moves at a snail’s pace even after a year of the incident, and the talks on restoration of democracy have broken down, the U.T. administration is moving at rocket speed to conduct some kind of council elections here, apparently to have people of their choice installed to negotiate on democracy and safeguards here,” said Mr. Wancghuk.

articles.title: Two days past Deepavali, NPCI yet to announce a date for UPI MDR rollout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: About a month ago, when the NPCI had pushed back the rollout of MDR from its original date of October 15, it had said it would be implemented “immediately post Diwali”

Two days since Deepavali, the National Payments Council of India is yet to notify a new date for the implementation of the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions and The Hindu has learnt that “there is no announcement on this at the moment”.

When it had put the proposed additional charge on hold nearly a month ago, the NPCI had said the new date would be announced “immediately” after Deepavali. The new rate was originally supposed to have been implemented on October 15.
“There is no announcement on this at the moment,” a spokesperson at the NPCI told The Hindu when asked whether the NPCI’s date announcement was imminent.

The matter of an MDR levy on specified UPI transactions received significant pushback from merchants and petrol pump dealers alike, apart from customers who feared that merchants would pass on the extra charge on to them by way of higher prices.
The petrol pump dealers further said that the MDR charge, coupled with the fact that their dealer commission had not been revised in several years, meant that their margins would be further squeezed.

The NPCI had on October 13 announced that its UPI and Services Steering Committee had decided that “keeping in mind the festive season, Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions, shall be implemented immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately”.

The Hindu had at the time reported that, according to government sources, the decision to delay the implementation of MDR on UPI was made in the Prime Minister’s Office following strong appeals from traders.

Praveen Khandelwal, founder and secretary-general of the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) and a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Lok Sabha member, had welcomed the deferment, saying that it would protect traders’ interests and sustain digital payment momentum during the festive season.

articles.title: Militants ambush police vehicles in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 10 officers

fullParagraphs: Police say militants have ambushed vehicles carrying police officers in northwestern Pakistan, triggering a gunbattle that killed at least 10 officers
Militants ambushed vehicles carrying police officers in northwestern Pakistan on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), triggering a gunbattle that killed at least 10 officers, officials said.
The attack took place in Kohat, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, which borders Afghanistan, local police official Faisal Khan said.
He said two senior police officers were among the dead and an exchange of fire between security forces and the attackers was ongoing. He provided no further details.

Hours later, the Pakistani Taliban in a statement claimed the attack. The Pakistani Taliban, who were formerly known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, have stepped up attacks on security forces in the region in recent months.

Pakistan has seen a surge in violence in recent years, much of it blamed on the TTP. The group is separate from but closely allied with the Afghan Taliban, who returned to power in neighboring Afghanistan in 2021.
Pakistan frequently accuses Afghanistan’s Taliban government of sheltering TTP militants, an allegation Kabul denies.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier

The Democratic Republic of Congo's worst-ever outbreak of Ebola has now reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases, official Congolese figures showed on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), as armed conflict hampers the response.
The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier.
It has infected 11,042 people in the DRC and caused 5,387 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health.
Around 2,990 people have recovered from Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever.
Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years.
The worst outbreak previously recorded in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 people out of 3,500 cases between 2018 and 2020.
The latest outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu.
Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.
No approved vaccines or treatments exist currently for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the latest outbreak.

Last month, the World Health Organization announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, would be put through a full human trial in the DRC to see if it offered any cross-protection against Bundibugyo.

articles.title: Italy evacuates over 300 schools due to bomb alert, with threats in Scotland and Ireland
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni said there was no indication of any “concrete danger” to schools and that the threats appeared aimed at “generating alarm and concern”

Italian authorities evacuated hundreds of schools on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) after an emailed bomb threat, the latest in a series of disruptions affecting European institutions following recent hoaxes aimed at airlines and broadcasters.
Schools in Ireland, Scotland and Northern Ireland received similar threats, but no evacuations were reported.

Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni said there was no indication of any “concrete danger” to schools and that the threats appeared aimed at “generating alarm and concern”. She said investigations were underway and that she had called a meeting of ministers for later Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

The anonymous email also threatened Ms. Meloni, according to copies obtained by Italian media, including the LaPresse news agency. She did not address the personal threat in her statement, and her office had no immediate comment.

The email purported to come from the leader of an otherwise unknown group with an anti-woman name and contained particularly violent threats. It was signed with the same Russian name used in last week's threats against European broadcasters.
Authorities have not attributed the threats to any group or state, and no evidence has emerged linking the hoaxes to a government.

Police in Northern Ireland said they were conducting “urgent inquiries” after a threatening email was sent to hundreds of schools. Police in Scotland said they were treating similar messages as hoaxes and were not requiring schools to evacuate.
“Our assessment remains that they do not represent a credible threat,” Police Scotland said.
Police in Ireland also said they were aware of a “generic communication” sent to several educational institutions.
Italian Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara told reporters that 312 schools had been evacuated after receiving email threats.

articles.title: ‘Iran will not allow enriched nuclear material to leave the country’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Rezaei has ‌said ⁠there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran ⁠and Washington

Iran will not allow even a single ​particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country, and there ‌will be consequences in the event of any ​new U.S. strikes on the Islamic Republic, Iranian ⁠security chief Mohsen Rezaei said in televised remarks.

Mr. Rezaei was speaking to Lebanon's pro-Iranian Al Mayadeen TV after U.S. officials downplayed the need ‌for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting President Donald Trump's more conciliatory tone since the ‌Republicans' defeat in the November 3 midterm elections.
Mr. Rezaei has ‌said ⁠there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran ⁠and Washington.
"Any new U.S. attacks will also be met with targeting U.S. bases far away," he said.
Iran's Supreme Leader has issued a directive ​that the country's near-weapons-grade uranium ‌should not be sent abroad, two senior Iranian sources said in May.

"We need the enriched material to design ships and submarines that work on nuclear energy", Mr. Rezaei said, ‌adding that Tehran has informed Moscow that its enriched ​nuclear material will remain in the country and "we will use it ourselves".
Russia has previously offered to ⁠remove uranium from Iran as part of a potential deal to ease U.S. concerns, but said it was for Tehran to ‌decide whether to remove it or not.

The IAEA estimates that Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60% — a level far higher than needed for civilian use — when Israel and the U.S. attacked Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025. How much of that has survived is ‌unclear.
Israel, the United States and other Western countries have long accused Iran ​of seeking nuclear weapons. Iran denies the accusation.
Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of ⁠any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the war between the ⁠two countries.

articles.title: Prix Pascal: If AI writes your book, are you still a writer?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: France’s new Prix Pascal for AI-assisted books prompts a writer to reflect on the slow pleasures of making art, loss of individuality, and need to reclaim human imagination

There is now a new French literary prize for AI-assisted writing — the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA. The Pascal prize requires entrants to turn in an unpublished manuscript, fiction or non-fiction, in French, of approximately 3,00,000 characters, written with the help of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Writers must declare which AI model and prompts they have employed. The applications, to be submitted by November 30, consist of “a seed, a manuscript and a technical file, submitted simultaneously”. Ten finalists will be announced on December 4 and the winner will be revealed on December 15.

“This [submitted] work must be useful, or raise awareness, or help to solve in an original way one of the ecological, social and ethical challenges that threaten humanity. AI can now solve previously unsolvable mathematical problems. Here, it is asked to produce a text that will help humanity progress towards wisdom and the preservation of itself and its environment.”

I love the way in which the manifesto strategically reframes tacit support for what goes against the very grain of the creative spirit as an essentially moral and ethical act. But of course! This is the way these things are usually done. The prize was founded by Philippe Rodriguez, Albin Serviant and Gilles Mentré. The first two are technology entrepreneurs, which too is no surprise.

Notwithstanding their precarity, writers and artists have always been viewed with a combination of envy, fear and hatred. The imagination is a dangerous thing. It is ungovernable. It cannot easily be controlled or colonised. It does not seek permission. And that, to many, is frightening. What better way to colonise the imagination than to introduce AI into the writer’s world? Also, that way everybody — even the ones with little understanding of what a writer does — can acquire the overnight label of one. Where does this leave writers who have spent years honing their craft, writers who have survived by the skin of their teeth? The world needs writers more urgently than ever before, and more of us should let some form of creative practice into our lives.

Two semesters ago, a few students from my Creative Writing course, at Shiv Nadar University, Chennai, confessed to what their worst fears were: that, having come of age in the post-AI era, they would find it a challenge to access and exercise their imagination — which, in their understanding, was foundational to the course. I was struck by their capacity for self-reflection, moved by what they recognised, quite rightly, as an imminent loss. This, too, is the other dark side of what we have got ourselves into: the loss of imagination is foundational not just to the stray creative writing course but to life itself.

The argument that it is best not to be left behind, that AI is here to stay so writers must take the good things it has to offer and navigate the rest, is a specious one. The folks making this argument may be right about the inevitability of AI, but does that make any of it less disturbing or a tad more ethical? I don’t see how one can frame this as anything other than a pure black-and-white story. If you give AI an inch, it is very likely that you will take a mile from yourself.

It is a slippery slope. You start by using AI as an instrument — perhaps to help you rewrite a sentence — and before you know it, you are likely to seek its help extensively to write the entire piece. Who then is the real author of the piece? After all, it is in the writing that writers do their thinking. I don’t think the answer lies in declaring AI use upfront. While this may address the ethical question to a small extent, it still does not change the fact that we are always going to ‘writing’ with training wheels on. The craft is in the writing and if you give that away what is left?

There is another problem too: that of the asymmetry between the writer on whose work an LLM is trained and the user who then draws on that work to write in “collaboration with” that particular AI model. The original writer whose consent has very likely not been sought gets nothing from this entire process — a process which de-humanises creative work and repurposes it as training data.

Artificial intelligence illustrations are seen on a lapto with books in the background in this illustration photo on 18 July, 2023. (Photo by Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | Photo Credit: Getty Images

As almost everyone from editors of literary journals on the brink of closure to writing teachers will tell you, it is often impossible to tell AI-assisted writing apart from human writing. In fact, you may find that some AI-assisted writing may be as good as if not better than writing by humans. It, of course, depends on the prompts used and how advanced the models are.

articles.title: Anaemia prevention in India: pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: If anaemia reduction should align with India’s goals for NCD reduction, then the focus must be on better diets through diversification. That should be non-negotiable for public health policy: no amount of papering over cracks with pills and potions will work in the long term

India has had decades of unchanged high anaemia prevalence in women and children that has historically been thought to be due to iron deficiency. This has led firstly to an iron and folic acid (IFA) tablet supplementation targeted at women and children, and secondly to fitful implementation of mandatory fortification of staple foods. IFA is a ‘precision’ strategy, applying as it does to the vulnerable population it is intended for, while fortification is a broad strategy that applies to the entire population. The latter works in controlled settings such as clinical trials, but has not worked in real-world settings, and might have adverse effects when given to those it is unintended for.

The reason for pivoting: anaemia is mistakenly conflated with iron deficiency In India. The evidence is otherwise: in national Indian surveys, it has been shown that iron deficiency is not the major cause of anaemia. Indeed, fully one-third of anaemia cases demonstrate no micronutrient deficiency or obvious cause. Even so, giving iron should have sorted out those who did have iron deficiency anaemia, and reduced the general anaemia prevalence. While this could be a problem with inefficient programme implementation, two important questions arise: is there is really a deficiency in dietary iron intake in India? And is the administered iron being adequately absorbed and utilised for haemoglobin formation?

Science, Space & Environment Report: Anaemia prevention in India: pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Ensure HYDRAA chief’s presence before Bench in contempt case: HC to DGP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana High Court, on Wednesday, directed Director General of Police C.V. Anand to ensure the presence of HYDRAA Commissioner and IPS officer A.V. Ranganath before a Bench on November 17 in a contempt of court case.

Earlier, Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy directed the HYDRAA Commissioner and Shamshabad Tahsildar to be present before the Bench on Wednesday, having issued Form-I notices to them. The Commissioner and the Tahsildar filed an interlocutory application seeking exemption from appearance. Not convinced by the reasons cited by the two officials, the judge directed the DGP to ensure their presence on November 17.

The Telangana High Court on Wednesday directed the Principal Secretary of Finance Sandeep Kumar Sultania to clear bills to the tune of ₹51.35 crore to be paid to persons whose lands were acquired by the government for various projects in Narayanpet district, within eight weeks.

Passing the direction, Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar instructed the officer to file a comprehensive additional affidavit explaining the payment mode and time required for clearing the remaining bills. The Principal Secretary, appearing before the Bench in virtual mode for hearing a batch of six contempt of court cases, informed that the State was in a precarious financial position and was not able to pay compensation at once to all the petitioners.
The judge observed that courts cannot be casual in contempt cases especially in matters connected to payment of compensation to citizens who gave away their lands for government projects.

The Telangana High Court on Wednesday issued notices to SPECTRA group entities in real estate business to respond to the contentions raised by Right Society in a PIL petition alleging that the group owners indulged in real estate scam.

Senior counsel B. Rachna Reddy appearing for the petitioner contended that the group owners took nearly 10,000 home buyers for a ride in Bhongir, Hyderabad, Shadnagar, Yadadri, Narkatpally, Balanagar and other areas.
The matter was adjourned to December 23 for next hearing.

The Telangana High Court, on Wednesday, directed Director General of Police C.V. Anand to ensure the presence of HYDRAA Commissioner and IPS officer A.V. Ranganath before a Bench on November 17 in a contempt of court case.

Earlier, Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy directed the HYDRAA Commissioner and Shamshabad Tahsildar to be present before the Bench on Wednesday, having issued Form-I notices to them. The Commissioner and the Tahsildar filed an interlocutory application seeking exemption from appearance. Not convinced by the reasons cited by the two officials, the judge directed the DGP to ensure their presence on November 17.

The Telangana High Court on Wednesday directed the Principal Secretary of Finance Sandeep Kumar Sultania to clear bills to the tune of ₹51.35 crore to be paid to persons whose lands were acquired by the government for various projects in Narayanpet district, within eight weeks.

Passing the direction, Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar instructed the officer to file a comprehensive additional affidavit explaining the payment mode and time required for clearing the remaining bills. The Principal Secretary, appearing before the Bench in virtual mode for hearing a batch of six contempt of court cases, informed that the State was in a precarious financial position and was not able to pay compensation at once to all the petitioners.

The judge observed that courts cannot be casual in contempt cases especially in matters connected to payment of compensation to citizens who gave away their lands for government projects.

The Telangana High Court on Wednesday issued notices to SPECTRA group entities in real estate business to respond to the contentions raised by Right Society in a PIL petition alleging that the group owners indulged in real estate scam.

Senior counsel B. Rachna Reddy appearing for the petitioner contended that the group owners took nearly 10,000 home buyers for a ride in Bhongir, Hyderabad, Shadnagar, Yadadri, Narkatpally, Balanagar and other areas.

The matter was adjourned to December 23 for next hearing.

articles.title: Lam Research conducts finale of nationwide semiconductor challenge at PES college
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: More than 800 teams, each comprising four students from multidisciplinary backgrounds, from 190 colleges, including IITs and leading NIRF-ranked engineering institutions, competed in Lam’s advanced systems engineering challenge

Lam Research, a supplier of wafer fabrication equipment, has brought students from several top engineering institutions in India under the Lam Research Challenge 2026, the California-based firm’s annual advanced semiconductor systems competition.

More than 800 teams, each comprising four students from multidisciplinary backgrounds, from 190 colleges, including IITs and leading NIRF-ranked engineering institutions, competed in Lam’s advanced systems engineering challenge. The participation underscored the growing importance of systems engineering skills needed to design, build and optimise increasingly complex semiconductor manufacturing technologies.

Following a multi-stage, three-month competition that included qualification and hardware-build rounds, selected teams advanced to the finale. The winners were announced at the grand finale held at PES University in Bengaluru.
During the finale, participants developed solutions to complex technical challenges, demonstrating creativity, engineering execution and the ability to translate ideas into working outcomes.

According to Lam Research, entries were evaluated on innovation, technical excellence, collaboration, problem-solving and performance under pressure, with IIT Guwahati emerging as the overall winner. IIT Ropar finished runner-up and NIT Calicut second runner-up. The winners shared prize money worth ₹10 lakh, while select students were offered internship opportunities with Lam Research.

“Semiconductor manufacturing is one of the most sophisticated engineering environments in the world today, requiring talent that can solve complex, systems-level challenges,” said Rangesh Raghavan, Corporate Vice President and Managing Director, Lam Research India.
According to Mr. Raghavan, the Lam Research Challenge is designed to help students build capabilities while gaining exposure to the kinds of engineering problems shaping the future of the industry.

He said advanced semiconductor manufacturing requires expertise spanning hardware, software, automation, data science, process engineering and advanced controls, making systems engineering a critical capability for the industry’s future growth. Unlike traditional engineering competitions focused on individual disciplines, the Lam Research Challenge encourages participants to apply systems-level thinking and understand how multiple technologies and functions interact within large-scale manufacturing operations, the company said.

Mr. Raghavan said the industry’s talent requirements are evolving beyond traditional engineering disciplines. Modern semiconductor manufacturing environments require engineers who can understand and optimise entire systems rather than individual components in isolation, creating growing demand for talent capable of integrating technologies across increasingly complex engineering environments.

Building the pipeline of future talent continues to be important as India expands its role across semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, equipment engineering and the broader electronics ecosystem, he added.

articles.title: Three Namma Metro Pink Line stations to be renamed

Both said the changes were approved in response to public demands and on the recommendation of a committee of which Mr. Surya was a member.

The request was jointly submitted by elected representatives, including Forest, Ecology and Environment Minister Ramalinga Reddy, Mr. Gowda, Mr. Surya and MLAs Satish Reddy, Uday Garudachar and M. Krishnappa.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. 1. Core Context & Background: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamil Nadu / government / politics / language / Delimitation / education / Governor / taxes and duties / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / Bharatiya Janata Party
